News.title: Randy couple caught romping on park bench by horrified passer-by who found them naked from waist down
News.content:
SICK ACT Randy couple caught romping on park bench by horrified passer-by who found them naked from waist down

A RANDY couple were caught romping on a park bench by a horrified passer-by who found them naked from the waist down, a court heard.

Katy McKay, 42, and 43-year old Kelvin Murray, 43, were on a stroll when they engaged in the steamy session.



But the amorous couple were caught out when a passer-by wandered past the bench and reported them to police.

Officers arrived at Queens Park in Warrington, Cheshire, to find the pair naked from the waist down with their privates exposed.



McKay hurriedly pulled her trousers up when the police approached.

When quizzed, the couple promised they would ”not be doing it again” and claimed it was so dark they didn’t realise they would be seen.



McKay and Murray, who are understood to have since split up, pleaded guilty to outraging public decency.

They were fined £320 with £213 in costs and a surcharge.

Warrington Magistrates’ Court was told the romp took place on July 26 at 11pm after the pair had been out for the evening.

Teri O’Brien, prosecuting, said: “Police were made aware of a report of a male and female seen to be having sex in Queens Park.



“En route the officers received a further report from the reporting person, that the genitals of both the male and female could be seen.

“The incident was also captured by local authority CCTV. On arrival the defendant Miss McKay was present with the other defendant Mr Murray on a bench.

“PC Rimmer and PC Ballantyne approached the defendants. Miss McKay was exposing her genitals. As the officers approached she pulled her trousers up.”



Defence solicitor Mark Lever suggested in mitigation that as it was dark, the couple may have assumed no one would see them.

He added: “It was late for that area. They are both very sorry. They apologise to the court for their behaviour. I am sure they won’t do something like this again.”

Sentencing the pair, JP Dr Gwyneth Edwards said: “You have pleaded guilty to this offence – but you could hardly not.

“It was a very reckless act and it was in public.”

News.title: Second man arrested for ‘arson’ after inferno destroyed 140 cars at Gatwick Airport parking site
News.content:
COPS have arrested a second man on suspicion of arson after a savage blaze ripped through 140 vehicles at a Gatwick Airport parking site.

Police and firefighters scrambled to the scene of the blaze at Caldyne Business Park in Rowfant, West Sussex, just after 9pm on Saturday.



Thick black smoke poured into the night sky as the powerful blaze ripped through the site.

Drivers were “left in the dark” as they desperately tried to find out if their vehicles had been caught up in the blaze.



Shocking images of the aftermath showed rows of charred, unrecognisable cars.

It is understood that the site is predominantly used for people parking their cars and heading to Gatwick Airport.



A 67-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of arson on Saturday.

Cops have arrested a second man, 29, on the same charge.



UK Power Network confirmed it was forced to shut off power to more than 2,000 homes while crews tackled the incident at the industrial estate.

A West Sussex Fire & Rescue Service spokeswoman confirmed that “approximately 140 vehicles were destroyed in the fire”.

Worried drivers told The Sun they were unable to contact the parking company and have no idea if their cars are damaged or not.

Sam and George Smith, 51 and 53, said they paid £105 to Sapphire Parking through an app last week.



He said they were told their car is fine but later were informed the company couldn’t access the site as it’s cordoned off.

“So I don’t know how he’d know that. I think they’re fobbing people off… most of the cars are unrecognizable anyway.

“You can’t tell if your car is destroyed or not. We’re in the dark, we don’t know anything.”

Other worried customers posted on social media saying they couldn’t get through to the company to find out if their cars were caught up in the inferno.



A Sapphire Parking spokesperson told The Sun: “The police and fire service are currently preventing anyone from entering the compound due to ongoing safety concerns, as they have not yet been able to establish whether any hazardous materials or objects remain within the site.

What are your rights if your car is damaged in a fire? Whether you can claim money depends on a number of factors Liability depends on where the fire started, which must be established through a technical expert assessment. Only once that investigation is complete can it be clear which insurer is responsible for compensating the losses. If the investigation finds that the fire began in the vehicle itself, the insurance policies linked to that vehicle come into play. But your car is damaged in an accident – like a fire – your insurance company will assess the damage and decide whether your car should be written off. If your car is written off, your insurer will typically pay you the market value of your car just before the accident or damage occurred, minus your policy excess and any outstanding finance. However, if the fire is traced to a fault in the building’s electrical installation, a charging point, or any other fixed garage infrastructure, liability may fall on the building’s management. For example, this could be the residents’ management company or on the entity responsible for installing and maintaining that equipment. Where the fire damages other cars, the garage structure or third-party property, liability has to be assessed on a case-by-case basis. Exactly the same principles apply to electric vehicles. It depends if the fire began in the high-voltage battery or another component of the car. However, if the vehicle was connected to a charging point, the investigation must also determine whether the fire started in the car or in the charging infrastructure.

“We have been advised that we should be able to gain access to the compound on Tuesday, subject to clearance from the relevant authorities.

Once we are permitted to enter, we will immediately assess the vehicles and the extent of the damage.

“At that point, we will be in a position to provide our customers with accurate information regarding their vehicles and the impact of the fire.

We sincerely apologise for the uncertainty and inconvenience this situation is causing.

“Please be assured that we will update you as soon as we have access to the site and have been able to complete our initial assessment.”

The cause of the fire is unclear, but fire services say it involved a workshop, electric and heavy goods vehicles and cylinders.



Nearby residents were advised over the weekend to keep windows and doors closed and members of the public were also asked to avoid the area.

No one was injured in the fire, which roared well into the early hours.

The car park is often used by holidaymakers, those staying at nearby holiday parks and local businesses.

A London Gatwick spokesperson said: “We are aware of a fire at an unaffiliated third-party car parking site, which occurred on Saturday evening, and understand how concerning and distressing this will be for any passengers whose vehicles may have been affected.

News.title: Reading Festival announces last-minute rule change as Met Office issues thunderstorm warning
News.content:
READING Festival has made a last-minute rule change as it prepares to kick off tomorrow.

The huge event will welcome around 100,000 music lovers over the next few days – and there’s been a change they’ll need to know about.



Reading Festival has backtracked on its plans to ban camping stoves from the event, following UK wildfires this summer.

After weeks of drought and hosepipe bans across the nation, festival organisers put camping stoves on the prohibited items list.



However, after the arrival of rainier weather in parts of England and thunderstorms forecast, it has been confirmed that specific stoves will now be permitted.

In a statement, Reading Festival said: “Reading festival have decided that due to the change in weather conditions, camping stoves compliant with the ‘What You Can and Can’t Bring’ section of the website will be permitted into the campsites.”

The announcement continued: “Only permitted types of camping stoves will be allowed, so please take time to check the requirements in advance or your stove may not be allowed in.”

The guidelines for stoves that will be allowed into the campsites at the festival outline that only certain types and certain fuels are acceptable.

Meth stoves, Trangia stoves, solid fuel stoves, hexamine stoves, gel stoves, firelighter stoves and flat-based gas camping stoves can be brought.

However, campfires and disposable barbecues are strictly forbidden, along with fire pits and any other charcoal barbecue.



Festival bosses said: “Reminder: Disposable BBQs are not permitted on site. Please do not bring them.

“Campfires are not permitted and anyone found lighting one will be evicted.”

Festivalgoers have also been warned against dropping cigarettes on the floor and told to be mindful of cigarette butt disposal.

Blowtorches, candles, incense, paper lanterns and fireworks are also banned.

News.title: Horror moment mudslide wipes out border crossing ‘with no way to escape’ as rescuers search for survivors
News.content:
THIS is the horror moment a mudslide crashes onto a building and traps dozens who are feared dead.

Authorities have reported “major casualties” with several people missing after the disaster wiped out a land crossing between China and Nepal.



Shocking footage shows a huge wave of debris surge through a building which crashes to the ground in a terrifying cloud of dust.

Terrified residents can be spotted running for their lives as the mudslide surged across the border from Nepal into China.



“A mudslide disaster on the Nepalese side resulted in major casualties and missing people at the Gyirong Port” said Chinese state TV.

President Xi Jinping had urged “all-out” rescue operations as emergency crews scrambled to rescue people trapped in the rubble.

He said: “The most urgent task is doing everything possible to search for and rescue the missing people… quickly treat injured people and minimise casualties to the greatest extent possible”.

The entire region of Shigatse was plunged into darkness as the mudslide slashed through power cables.

Nepal has also been devastated after flash floods ripped through several villages and killed at least eight people.

The river Lende in Nepal broke its banks and surged across dozens of homes as residents fled for their lives.



One witness told CNN: “It all came suddenly.

“We heard a loud sound, like a volcano erupting. People started to scream and ran away.”

The waters were so high that rescue helicopters struggled to land, according to army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet.

News.title: Ban on first cousin marriages ‘considered by Labour’ over fears weddings are being used to ‘bypass the system’
News.content:
WEDDING BAN Ban on first cousin marriages ‘considered by Labour’ over fears weddings are being used to ‘bypass the system’

LABOUR is considering whether to back legislation banning first-cousin marriage in the United Kingdom, amid fears that weddings are being used to “bypass the system”.

The Ministry of Justice acknowledged serious concerns surrounding cousin unions, confirming it will examine whether a complete ban represents the most effective response.

Shadow health minister Dr Luke Evans is set to introduce a backbench bill in Parliament early next year in a renewed effort to outlaw the practice.

A previous attempt by shadow transport secretary Richard Holden stalled when Sir Keir Starmer’s government blocked his private member’s bill last year.





Mr Holden has since called on PM Andy Burnham to not be “unwilling” in supporting the upcoming proposals.

While first-cousin unions represent under one per cent of total marriages nationwide, research indicates significantly higher rates within specific communities.

Data from the Born in Bradford health study suggests that between 35 and 55 per cent of British individuals of Pakistani heritage marry a first cousin.

The same study highlighted distinct developmental and health disparities.

Controlling for socioeconomic factors such as poverty, children born to first cousins in Bradford faced an 11 per cent risk of speech and language issues, compared to seven per cent for children of unrelated parents.

Furthermore, 54 per cent of children of first cousins achieved a “good stage of development” – the government’s baseline assessment for five-year-olds in England – compared to 64 per cent among children of non-relatives.

Mr Holden told GB News: “Given cases like this, it’s quite clear to me that first cousin marriage is now being used as a way to try and bypass the normal immigration system, and it’s pretty clear to me that we need to act more swiftly than that.

“I want to see the Government backing the bill that Dr Evans is bringing forward, just get on board with it.



“This is something that whether you’re a Conservative voter or a Labour voter or a Reform voter or a liberal voter, actually right across the board, people want to see first cousin marriage banned.”

He said Labour was “unwilling to face down certain voices within certain communities”.

Mr Holden added: “The truth is that I’ve had genuinely dozens of messages from people within the British-Pakistani community saying, ‘Richard, please keep going on this campaign. It’s very difficult for us to speak out’.

“But actually they’re telling me that those opinion polls, which show that the majority of British-Pakistanis want to see this banned as well, are true.

“And they’re saying it’s just the Government is unwilling to stand up to certain vested interests within parts of the British-Pakistani community.



“The Government should be on the side of the people, not on the side of some of these so-called community leaders.”

Britain remains an outlier compared to several international peers regarding cousin marriage.

Norway introduced a complete prohibition on cousin marriage in 2024 while Sweden’s ban takes effect this year.

In the United States, 32 states prohibit first-cousin marriage, with eight defining the act as a criminal offence.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

An MoJ spokesman said: “We recognise the serious concerns that have been raised around this issue.



“As any responsible government would do, we must look at whether legislation is the best solution to tackle this.”

News.title: Two missing in huge house fire feared to be ‘gangland revenge attack’ linked to five ‘joyriders’ killed in A66 crash
News.content:
AT LEAST two people are missing presumed dead after a fire tore through a house in the wake of the A66 crash that left seven dead, including two cops.

Firearms officers stood guard at the scene of the blaze this morning amid fears it is part of a gangland revenge attack following Saturday’s horror smash.



Five youths – Michael Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, and 17-year-old Cole Worthy – died after driving the wrong way down the dual carriageway.

They were trying to shake-off police after a high-speed pursuit when they headed towards oncoming traffic near Middlesbrough.



Police abandoned their pursuit but 10 seconds later their VW Passat ploughed into an armed response unit.

Firearms officers – married dad-of-two PC Matthew Blades, 37, and Iraq war hero PC Tom Clough, 38 – were killed instantly.



Cops believe the Passat gang were out looking for revenge after the home belonging to Worthy’s dad was rammed twice by a Volvo XC60 minutes earlier.

It reversed twice into the front window at 3am on Saturday.



There is no suggestion the 17-year-old’s dad, Gye, 39, was involved in criminal activity.

But police believe it may have provided the flashpoint for the events that unfolded in the minutes leading up to the 3:39am crash.

There are now fears the latest incident could be linked to an explosion of gang warfare in Middlesbrough.

Police, ambulance, fire and rescue and Northern Gas Networks remain at the scene of the blaze on Birchington Avenue, Grangetown.

Shocked residents said two people were missing, while two others had been able to escape from the house.



One neighbour said: “Some people got out, and a few people did not. It’s tragic.”

A relative of the family who lived in the house, which has lost its roof in the blaze, also confirmed two people had escaped, while another two were missing.

Ciara Randle, 10, said: “I woke up to screaming, dogs barking and sirens, very early. The sun had only just come up.



“I told my mum as soon as we got up, and we realised there had been a fire. We’re very shocked.

“The fire had been put out by then, but there was smoke, and the house was smouldering.”

Ciara’s mum Theresa Randle, a 42-year-old carer added: “We don’t know the people in the house very well, but we say hello to them.



“The poor family. We feel so sad for them.

“By the time we got up, the fire had been put out. We don’t know what happened.

“It’s a tragedy, especially so soon after the crash at the weekend.”

Cleveland Fire Brigade said it was called to the blaze at 05:23 this morning.

A spokesperson added: “Crews are currently dealing with the incident, with six fire engines and the Incident Command Unit at the scene.



“Road closures are in place in the surrounding area, and Cleveland Fire Brigade are asking members of the public to avoid the area where possible to allow emergency services to work safely.

“The incident remains ongoing, and further updates will be provided when available.”

A spokesperson for Cleveland Police said: “Birchington Avenue and Leighton Road in Grangetown is currently closed while officers and emergency services respond to a fire at the property.



“Please avoid the area and use alternative routes.”

Cleveland Police said that four of those killed in the vehicle – Worthy, Matusiak, Saddington and Rae – which hit the cop car had previous police convictions.

All four had appeared in court charged with a series of offences.

Saddington pleaded guilty to possession of a Class C drug and a knife in May 2025 and months later admitted three offences of assaulting a police officer.

Meanwhile, Worthy admitted using threatening and abusive language to cause harassment, alarm and distress in October 2024.



In March, Matusiak admitted using a vehicle without insurance and driving without a licence.



While, Rae was convicted of assaulting a police officer, shoplifting, stealing cars, theft, drug possession and breaching a youth rehabilitation order.

Cops have also confirmed that nine men and three women aged between 19 and 61, have been arrested on suspicion of several offences in connection with the crash.

The alleged offences include possession of a firearm and participating in the activities of an organised crime group.

A further five men, aged 16 to 55, were then arrested yesterday in connection with the crash – bringing the total to seventeen in custody.

Some of those arrested over the A66 investigation are suspected of “participating in the activities of an organised crime group” Cleveland Police added.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cops are continuing to investigate the moments leading up to the fatal smash on Saturday with National Crime Agency officers joining the probe.

Two of those arrested, aged 19 and 26, have since appeared in court charged with possession of a firearm, drug dealing and possession of stolen property while a third has been recalled to prison.

News.title: Tesco urgently recalls ‘contaminated’ salad over E. coli fears – and tells shoppers ‘don’t eat it’
News.content:
TESCO has urged shoppers not to eat a popular lunchtime staple following fears of a potential E.coli contamination.

Those experiencing symptoms have been advised to “stay away” from school and work.

Tesco‘s Finest Mozzarella Pearls & Pesto Orzo Salad has been urgently recalled after the possible presence of E.coli (STEC) was found.



The retailer said that batches with the best before dates of August 25, 26 and 27 had been affected, and advised shoppers to “not eat” the product.



In a written statement, Tesco said: “Tesco is recalling specific dates codes of Tesco Finest Mozzarella Pearls & Pesto Orzo Salad 215g, due to the possible presence of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC), which if consumed can cause illness.”

The Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC) strain can cause serious illness, incluidng bloody diarrhoea, abdominal pain and vomiting or low fever.

As a result, customers who may be experiencing the following side effects have been urged to “stay away from work, school or nursery” for at least 48 hours to avoid passing the illness to others, according to the Food Standards Agency.

Shoppers are able to return the product to any Tesco store for a full refund, with no receipt required.

Alternatively, they are also able to contact the support team for more information.

Tesco said it was “sorry for the inconvenience caused” and that no other products had been affected by the recall.

This comes as a number of products have issued similar recalls over the presence of E.coli in the past month, including Summit Food wraps and Rupunzel’s BionSnacky seed toppers.



If you start experiencing severe symptoms, please contact a medical professional immediately.

News.title: Terrifying moment plane goes up in flames midair as pilot desperately activates parachute before crashing in fireball
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a plane catches fire in mid-air before bursting into flames on the ground.

The footage shows the pilot deploying a parachute from the smoking single-engine plane to avoid a fatal landing in Greater Belo Horizonte, Brazil.



With black smoke trailing behind, the aircraft spirals in the air, and then explodes into an inferno in a wooded area.

The pilot, 29, miraculously survived and bystanders pulled him out the wreckage, according to firefighters.



He was rushed to the emergency care unit in Mateus Leme and then transferred to Hospital João XXIII in Belo Horizonte, the state’s capital.

It has been reported that he is suffering from suspected smoke inhalation.



The plane departed from Pampulha Airport at around 7:34am on Tuesday morning but was forced to make an emergency landing at 7:49am.

Motiva, the operator who runs Pampulha Airport said: “During the operation, there was no communication between the pilot and the Pampulha Airport Control Tower reporting any emergency, malfunction, or other incident.”

The plane appeared to be in normal status, according to the Brazilian Aeronautical Registry.

It even had a valid Airworthiness Verification Certificate until September 26, 2026.



The plane is a Cirrus SR22 model aircraft – also known as the ‘Ferrari of Airplanes’ to experts – where one of its uncommon safety systems is its parachute, where the pilot remains inside the aircraft.

The Cirrus Airframe Parachute System (CAPS) is designed specifically for these emergency situations.

Activation involves the deployment of a parachute to slow the plane down, reducing the chance of a devastating ground impact.



As of July this year, the CAPS system in the Cirrus aircraft has saved 302 people in these types of incidents, according to the Cirrus Owners and Pilots Association.

The Sun has contacted Motiva to find out why the plane had caught fire in the first place.

News.title: New Aldi £5 'anti-redness' skincare item similar to £34 Boots option out Sunday

New Aldi £5 'anti-redness' skincare item similar to £34 Boots option out Sunday

Beauty fans may be familiar with the £34 option at Boots, and Aldi will be bringing out its own similar version this weekend

View 3 Images The new items will be arriving in stores on Sunday (Image: Getty)

Aldi will soon release a new skincare item that could be a budget-friendly alternative for anyone who usually buys a similar product at Boots. The supermarket regularly updates its Special Buy deals on Thursdays and Sundays for Middle Aisle customers, and its upcoming product range may interest beauty fans.

‌



As part of a new 'Health and Beauty' collection coming out this Sunday, August 30, Aldi shoppers will be able to get their hands on a bottle of 'anti-redness' serum. Aldi's Lacura Colour Correcting Drops will be available in stores for £4.99.

‌



The drops could be a more affordable option for shoppers who usually opt for Dr Jart+ Cicapair Intensive Soothing Repair Serum, which currently costs £33.60 in Boots for a 30ml bottle. It is usually £42, but the high street store has it on offer right now.

‌



Similar to the Dr Jart product, Aldi's £4.99 drops are designed to help "reduce the look of redness" and "even your complexion". It is made with tiger grass extract, arnica extract and niacinamide. It also offers SPF 30.

The product description on Aldi's website adds: " Perfectly adapts to your natural skin colour to help cover blemishes, reduce the look of redness and even your complexion. Tiger grass extract. Arnica extract. Panthenol and vitamin B3."

View 3 Images Aldi's Lacura Colour Correcting Drops and Treatment (Image: Aldi)

‌



The active compounds in tiger grass extract, such as madecassoside and asiaticoside, are said to help reduce inflammation and calm sensitive or reactive skin. Tiger grass extract is also said to help lock in moisture, block out daily irritants, and speed up skin recovery from minor wounds, blemishes, and post-procedure irritation.

It is up to shoppers whether they prefer Aldi's £499 version or Boots' £34 Dr Jart option; however, one is more affordable for shoppers on a budget. On Boots website, a description of the serum reads: "A lightweight, yet potent serum enriched with Centella Asiatica extract and Peptides to effectively soothe, while rapidly boosting the all-important skin barrier, keeping the look of sensitivity at bay. News.title: Councils in England given permission to introduce bumper council tax rises next year - full list
News.content:
Councils in England given permission to introduce bumper council tax rises next year - full list

The maximum amount most councils in England can normally raise bills without a referendum is 5% - but six councils have been granted powers to introduce bigger hikes

View 2 Images Thousands of households look set to be hit with bumper council tax rises (Image: Drazen Zigic via Getty Images)

Hundreds of thousands of households face bumper council tax rises next year after six councils were given permission to raise costs by more than the usual amount.

‌



The maximum amount most councils in England can normally raise bills without a referendum is 5%. But Westminster, Kensington and Chelsea, Hammersmith and Fulham, City of London and Windsor and Maidenhead have been granted powers to introduce bigger rises.

‌



Wandsworth Council is said to be considering a council tax hike of up to 160% - in what would be the biggest increase ever in England. It currently has the lowest Band D council tax bills at £1,028 - in comparison, the average Band D council tax bill across England is £2,392.

‌



View 2 Images Council tax bills normally go up by 5% every April (Image: Getty)

HMRC sending out inspectors to value homes - and you may be hit with tax bill READ MORE :

The Telegraph reported earlier this month that Westminster council is considering raising council tax by 100%. The standard Band D council tax bill in Westminster is currently £1,049. However, no formal announcement or decision from any of the councils have been made yet.

Council tax decisions would likely come later this year, or early next year, and any increases would come into effect from April 2027. It follows a review into how funding from the central government is distributed among local councils, with more cash set to be issued to deprived areas.

‌



For example, Wandsworth is projected to receive £84million less a year by the end of the decade, while Westminster Council is set to lose £100million. Meanwhile, Windsor and Maidenhead were allowed to raise council tax by 7.49% this April to tackle severe budget deficits and stave off effective bankruptcy.

‌



What do the councils say?

Councillor Elizabeth Campbell, Leader of Kensington and Chelsea Council, said: “We will do everything we can to protect the services our residents value the most, but central Government has cut our funding by more than £100 million – a hole which cannot be plugged with just a simple council tax rise.

“We will still need to make significant savings, on top of the £21 million already agreed for this year. Alongside residents, we are still asking Government to rethink and revisit the approach they are taking – which penalises London and Londoners unfairly.”

Councillor Paul Fisher, Cabinet Member for Value for Money and Finance at Westminster Council, said: "It's so important that residents and businesses respond. The decisions we have to take next year will have major implications for years to come, including what increase in council tax gets proposed.

‌



"These UK Government funding cuts are unprecedented and present us with stark choices and no easy options. That’s why we need to ask our residents some straight questions - what council services do they care most about, and would they be prepared to pay more in Council Tax to offer some protection against service cuts."

Councillor Lynne Jones, Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for Finance at Windsor and Maidenhead Council, said: “We have worked hard to strengthen governance, restore financial discipline and improve the council’s financial position – progress that has been recognised by both government and through independent scrutiny, and we remain committed to continuing that journey.

"We had a credible plan that would have returned us back to financial sustainability, but that plan has been derailed by a further £30m budget reduction imposed by government."

‌



Wandsworth Council and City of London Council declined to comment. Hammersmith and Fulham Council did not respond to requests for comment. A spokesperson from the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said: "Decisions on whether to increase council tax are ultimately for local authorities to make and justify but we continue to expect any decisions to put taxpayers first."

The biggest council tax increases before this were by North Somerset, Shropshire and Worcestershire, who were all given special permission to enforce a 9% rise this April.

Cut your council tax bill

Check if you are entitled to a council tax discount. For example, if you live alone, you get 25% off your council tax bill. The maximum 100% discount is awarded if someone lives alone is considered to be "severely mentally impairment" and is claiming benefits, or if you live in an all-student household.

Article continues below

There are also Council Tax Support or Council Tax Reduction schemes for people claiming benefits or on low incomes. The exact help varies between councils but your bill could be reduced by up to 100%.

Not everyone is in the right council tax band - and if you're accidentally in too high of a band, you could be owed thousands of pounds back, plus lower bills going forward. But do your research, as if you're in too low of a band, you could get moved up and your bills will become more expensive. Your neighbours could also end up being bumped up.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal £50m agreement, Man Utd land huge boost, Barcola to Liverpool
News.content:
Newcastle United transfer target snubs Magpies

Former Chelsea star Christopher Nkunku has secured a loan move to former club RB Leipzig. The former Chelsea ace had been linked with a move to Newcastle United this summer.

Instead, he chose to move back to Leipzig, the club he became a European star which earned him a big money move to Chelsea. The Frenchman was sold to AC Milan last summer for £32million.

His return to Germany also includes a £25m option to buy. After sealing his return, he said: "When I heard of the opportunity to join RB Leipzig, I immediately wanted to say yes,” said Nkunku. “I'm very happy to be back here. I'm in excellent shape and want to help the team as soon as possible, and I also can't wait to once again play in front of our fans at the Red Bull Arena.

"My connection to RB Leipzig is very special. Even after leaving the club, I continued to keep a close eye on what was happening here. I'm now ready to add a new chapter to my time here at RBL. During my discussions with the club,

"I could sense just how much the people in charge here still value me and how much trust they have in me. That's why Leipzig is exactly the right place for me to perform to my best.”

News.title: Fussy Brits hauling hotel-grade mattresses, air fryers and hot tubs on camping trips
News.content:
Fussy Brits hauling hotel-grade mattresses, air fryers and hot tubs on camping trips

We don't like roughing it, according to research by Argos, which found campers prioritising home comforts over survival gear, with 72% ditching the back-to-basics mentality

View 2 Images We like camping, but want our home comforts - stock photo (Image: imageBROKER/Reinhard Pantke / Getty Images)

Fussy Brits are hauling hotel-grade mattresses, air fryers and hot tubs on camping trips to ensure a slice of luxury in the great outdoors, a study has revealed.

‌



Argos research reveals campers are prioritising home comforts over survival gear, with 72% ditching the back-to-basics mentality and going all-in on 'campmaxxing' this summer.

‌



A luxury-loving 15% said they'll be bringing their hotel-grade mattress with them while camping and 10% will be whipping up meals in their air fryers. A wacky 8% said they'd even pack their hot tub in a bid to create the ultimate outdoor set-up.

‌



View 2 Images Even hot tubs make it on to the must-have list for taking with us on outdoor holidays

UK weather maps show thunderstorms hitting 16 counties in just two hours – list READ MORE :

Calculate how much your energy bill will rise by as new Ofgem price cap announced READ MORE :

Of the 2,000 Brits quizzed, a spontaneous 63% say they'd pack a bag and head off on holiday with less than 24 hours' notice, while a third (32%) have already pulled off a last-minute escape.

The Argos study reveals this sudden urge for outdoor adventure is heavily driven by 'sensommer', the Scandinavian concept of 'late summer'.

‌



Two-fifths of Brits (41%) are embracing this mindset to stretch out the holiday season before autumn blues set in.

A whopping 50% of Gen Z and 54% of Millennials said the recent heatwaves have inspired them to book a late-summer or autumn camping trip in the UK.

But today's campers aren't settling for basic sleeping bags or disposable BBQs.

‌



Nearly three quarters (72%) planning a trip intend to splash out more than ever upgrading their pitch, with 42% prepared to spend more than £100 doing so.

It appears Brits are putting their hands in their pockets, as sales in the Argos camping category over the past five weeks are up almost 10% year-over-year on average.

The retailer also said it had seen a 60% surge in sales of camping chairs compared to the same five weeks of summer last year.

‌



A quarter (25%) of particular Brits admit they flat-out refuse to camp unless it feels boutique, with one-fifth (19%) trying to bring as many home comforts as possible.

Swapping surviving for thriving, just one in five (21%) Brits are back-to-basics camping traditionalists.

Instead, campers are embracing a more elevated take on the great outdoors, with 20% curating home-away-from-home comforts, 19% creating firepit-filled outdoor spaces, 17% taking high-end camping gear (17%) and 15% packing premium kitchen appliances.

‌



Brits' camping packing lists reflect the trend too, with holidaymakers planning to bring everything from a full dining table and chairs (21%) to mini fridges (21%) and gourmet portable BBQs (19%).

With Reading and Leeds Festival just around the corner, there's also a distinct festival vibe to Gen Z campers' set-ups, with 15% bringing high-spec speakers and 7% bringing full DJ decks.

Brits' Top 10 essentials for a luxury camping trip:

Al fresco dining sets (Full dining table and chairs) (21%)

‌



On-pitch mini fridges (21%)

‌



Cooling fans (21%)

Gourmet portable BBQs (19%)

‌



5, Surround-sound speakers (15%)

‌



6, Hotel-grade mattresses (15%)

Inflatable sofa and/or chairs (15%)

‌



Ambient fairy lights (13%)

‌



Outdoor rugs (12%)

10. Open-air TV or projector cinema screens (11%)

‌



Argos has curated a camping checklist, with thousands of products available the same day through its Click & Collect and Fast Track delivery services.

News.title: Officers injured as car 'rams police vehicle' after driving at 'high speed' in Belfast
News.content:
Officers injured as car 'rams police vehicle' after driving at 'high speed' in Belfast

Officers on patrol in Belfast spotted a silver Nissan Juke driving at high speed before it rammed a police vehicle 'a number of times' and injured the officers inside, the PSNI said

View Image Ballycolin Road on the outskirts of Belfast (Image: Google Maps)

Police have arrested two men after a car allegedly rammed a police vehicle, leaving two officers in need of hospital treatment.

The incident took place just before midnight on Tuesday when cops spotted a vehicle driving at speed in the Dunmurry area of west Belfast.

Officers on mobile patrol on the Glen Road spotted a silver Nissan Juke travelling at high speed and signalled for it to stop before the driver tried to force their way back onto the road, the PSNI said.

A PSNI spokesperson said: “The officers waited for a safe location before signalling for the car to stop, after it pulled into a laneway along the Ballycolin Road,” they said.

“The driver of the car, however, subsequently tried to force their way back onto the road, ramming the parked police vehicle a number of times in the process and injuring the two officers inside.

“They will now be attending hospital this morning, Wednesday 26th August, for treatment to their injuries.”

They said a 39-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of offences including attempted grievous bodily harm with intent, dangerous driving, driving when unfit through drink or drugs and possession of a class A controlled drug.

Meanwhile, a 44-year-old man was also arrested on suspicion of possession of a class A controlled drug.

Article continues below

Police have appealed for anyone who saw the car on Tuesday night, or who has any information which could assist, including dash-cam or other footage, to contact police using a witness appeal form at reporting.psni.police.uk/appeals, quoting reference 1771 of 25/08/26.

“You can also call us on 101 or contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111 or online at crimestoppers-uk.org/,” they added.

News.title: Passenger plane just feet away from hitting drone in near-miss over UK
News.content:
Passenger plane just feet away from hitting drone in near-miss over UK

The drone was flying at 5,500ft, almost 14 times the legal limit, and nearly crashed into a Virgin Atlantic plane carrying 264 passengers as it left Heathrow set for Johannesburg

View 3 Images There is growing concern about the use of drones near airports (Image: PA)

A Virgin Atlantic plane came just feet from hitting a drone flying at a height nearly 14 times the legal limit, a worrying new report shows.

‌



In a rare near-miss involving a passenger jet and the gadget in UK airspace, the incident presented a "serious" risk of collision. Pilots saw the contraption flying at around 5,500ft near Woking, Surrey, after departing Heathrow for Johannesburg, South Africa on June 8.

‌



A British Airprox Board report said crew spotted the drone too late to take avoiding action as it came within 16ft of crashing into the aircraft. The plane was carrying 264 passengers and the report comes amid growing concern about the use of the airborne devices near airports.

‌



A Virgin Atlantic spokesperson told the Mirror: "Virgin Atlantic can confirm that pilots operating flight VS449 from London Heathrow to Johannesburg on 8 June 2026 reported seeing a drone shortly after taking off from Heathrow.

View 3 Images The Virgin Atlantic plane was carrying hundreds of passengers and crew (Image: Getty Images)

Man found dead in plane's landing gear at Gatwick after suffering extreme cold READ MORE :

"The safety and security of our customers and crew is always our priority, and the pilots immediately reported the incident to Air Traffic Control in line with our procedures."

‌



Flying a drone in controlled airspace without authorisation is illegal and can carry significant penalties, including criminal charges. The operator was not found, but faces up to five years in prison if caught.

Drones, controlled by people from the ground or increasingly autonomously, are permitted to fly at a maximum height of 400ft in the UK. That means it was flying over 13 times the legal limit when it nearly collided with the aircraft.

Last year, the Mirror told how a drone came within '10m-20m' of colliding with a Boeing 737 airliner on its approach to Gatwick Airport.

‌



View 3 Images A drone can legally fly at a maximum height of 400ft (Image: PA)

The UKAB report rated it as the highest possible Category A incident, meaning there was a high chance of collision. The passenger plane was over Bexhill on Sea, east Sussex, on its approach to land at Gatwick, when the drone was spotted. The B737 Captain saw a black object in front of the aircraft and there was "no time to take avoiding action".

There have been repeated warnings from police about their use in and around airports and in public spaces. A new ray gun that uses high-frequency radio waves to blast them out of the sky has been successfully trialled by the Army.

Article continues below

Last April, footage emerged of the British Airways plane moments after it was hit by a suspected drone as it came into land at London's Heathrow Airport.

Video showed the BA727 flight full of 132 passengers and five crew from Geneva as it comes in for landing. British Airways said the aircraft was examined by engineers and cleared for its next flight following the incident.

News.title: Dragon's Den contestant who pitched eyeliner left half blind after medical blunder
News.content:
Dragon's Den contestant who pitched eyeliner left half blind after medical blunder

Noora Lewis says her life 'has completely changed' since losing the vision in her left eye

View 4 Images Noora Lewis, 63, has lost the sight in one of her eyes (Image: SWNS)

A Dragon’s Den contestant who pitched an eyeliner product is now partially blind after doctors failed to spot a devastating condition. Noora Lewis, 63, lost the sight in her left eye after doctors failed to diagnose giant cell arteritis (GCA), a condition that can cause irreversible blindness if not treated urgently.

The former make-up entrepreneur, who appeared on BBC One's Dragon's Den in 2012 with her beauty product "flick tips", repeatedly reported symptoms including headaches, jaw ache, tender temples, and pain on the right side of her face. After appointments at Birmingham and Midland Eye Centre and City Hospital, Noora was told she had inflammation in her eye and was sent home with steroids.

But her vision began to deteriorate before the condition was finally confirmed almost four months after she first sought medical help. By then, it was too late to save the sight in her left eye.

After losing her sight, Noora, from Birmingham, hired medical negligence lawyers Irwin Mitchell to investigate her care. Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust have now admitted a breach of duty saying there were failures in treating suspected giant cell arteritis.

View 4 Images Noora reported symptoms including headaches, jaw ache, tender temples, and pain on the right side of her face (Image: SWNS)

It also admitted that, with appropriate care, Noora would likely have avoided complications, including the impact on her vision. Lawyer Jenna Harris said: “Noora has been through a life-changing experience and is still struggling to adapt.

"The impact on her independence, ability to work, and emotional wellbeing has been significant."

Noora's lawyers are now working to negotiate a financial settlement with the NHS. Noora first attended Birmingham and Midland Eye Centre in May 2021 after two GP appointments and was diagnosed with uveitis, an inflammation inside the eye.

But her symptoms continued and the next month her GP suspected giant cell arteritis and told her to go to hospital immediately, warning she could go blind without the right treatment. At City Hospital, a doctor noted a lack of pulse in her right temporal artery, a key warning sign of the condition, but did not investigate further and discharged her after providing just a single day of steroid treatment.

She returned to City Hospital on June 14, where two doctors saw her but did not carry out any investigations into giant cell arteritis despite her ongoing symptoms and previous concerns. When Noora experienced visual disturbances in her left eye on July 25, she was admitted to City Hospital and spent three days undergoing tests.

Her diagnosis was finally confirmed on August 2, 2021. Noora, who has one grown-up child and four grandchildren, now struggles with everyday tasks and relies heavily on family and friends.

She said: “When I was finally diagnosed with giant cell arteritis, I felt angry. Thinking back, I had all the symptoms and can’t understand why I was left untreated for so long.”

View 4 Images Noora developed giant cell arteritis (Image: SWNS)

When she appeared on Dragon's Den in 2012 she failed to secure £50,000 of funding in exchange for 20 per cent of her Sensationelle business. Describing the devastating impact of losing her sight, Noora added: “My life has completely changed since losing my vision.

"The simplest tasks are now the hardest and I struggle with day-to-day things I used to take for granted, like shopping and using my phone, as letters and numbers appear distorted and can be very confusing.

“At times I even feel like a danger to myself - I’ve left the gas hob on without realising and now only drive very short distances, often having to rely on a friend or my daughter.”

View 4 Images Noora Lewis' eyeliner business (Image: SWNS)

The former self-employed make-up demonstrator said the condition had robbed her of her confidence and independence. She added: “I don’t feel like myself anymore. I used to be the fun one. I loved going out with friends or having people over for dinner, but I lack confidence now and find I’m much more anxious, which is so unlike me.

“By sharing my story, I hope to raise awareness of giant cell arteritis, symptoms to look out for, and the reality of people like me living with the condition.”

Dr Mark Anderson, group chief medical officer at the NHS trust, apologised to Noora. In a statement, he said: "We have acknowledged that aspects of the care provided fell below the standard we expect and have accepted liability in relation to those failings.

"We recognise the distress caused and the devastating effect that the loss of sight has had on her and her family, and have apologised for this."

News.title: Should Andy Burnham introduce rent controls? Take our poll and have your say
News.content:
Should Andy Burnham introduce rent controls? Take our poll and have your say

Andy Burnham is facing demands to introduce rent controls amid data showing tenants spend an average of 36.3% of their income on rent - have your say in our poll

View 2 Images Andy Burnham is facing demands to introduce rent controls (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham is facing demands to introduce rent controls amid data showing tenants spend an average of 36.3% of their income on rent.

‌



Dozens of MPs have written to Angela Rayner urging her to U-turn on her decision not to bring in rent controls in England. The Housing Secretary last month said the Government was not planning to bring in controls despite previous speculation.

‌



But new research showing tenants could save up to £1,418 a year if rent controls are introduced has reignited calls.

‌



The study, commissioned by the Joseph Rowntree Foundation (JRF) and carried out by the Autonomy Institute, tests three rent-control pathways introduced from 2027/28: a cap linked to inflation (CPI), a nominal freeze and a moderate approach that limits in-tenancy rises to inflation (CPI) and between-tenancy rises to inflation (CPI) plus 2%.

By 2031, per tenancy, tenants would be annually saving £1,418 if rents were frozen, £701 if moderate rent controls were brought in or £130 if CPI inflation-tracked rent controls were introduced, researchers said. The rent-control pathways are modelled alongside two other reforms: restoring full mortgage-interest deductions for landlords and applying National Insurance to landlord property income.

‌



The letter to Ms Rayner, organised by Labour MP Chris Hinchliff and signed by 26 MPs so far, backs the study and warns the Government it has an "opportunity to fix the foundations of our housing system for the long term".

It says: "On average rent now takes 36% of a renter’s salary, rising to almost half of their pay in some areas just to keep a roof over their heads. With so much of people’s income going on housing, it is little wonder that a third of renters are living in poverty.

"The impacts don’t stop at the front door either, when rent take up such a large chunk of a pay packet you aren’t able to spend in local cafés, restaurants or shops.

‌



View 2 Images Housing Secretary Angela Rayner last month said the Government was not planning to bring in controls despite previous speculation (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

"These extortionate rents are the elephant in the room when we talk about the cost of living. The Prime Minister is right to support a mass council housebuilding programme to lay the long-term foundations of a housing system based on meeting need. However, renters are feeling the pain of high rent today and rent controls are essential to easing that pressure."

It is signed by mostly Labour MPs plus a few Green MPs, as well as Your Party MP Jeremy Corbyn.

‌



In 2023, Mr Burnham - who was then the Greater Manchester mayor - called for freezes to private sector rents during the cost of living crisis. But Ms Rayner told the BBC last month: "I don't think that rent freezes, rent controls, is a way forward at the moment.

"Three years ago, Andy called for that because there was a significant crisis in the rental market. We implemented between then the Renters' Rights Act which is giving renters more power and control."

She added that controls had not "necessarily brought rents down" where they had been imposed in other places in the UK, such as Scotland. Other critics warn rent controls could increase the housing crisis by putting off people from renting out their house.

Article continues below

Nearly a fifth of UK households now rent privately, and high rents have strained living standards for two decades.

An MHCLG spokesman said: “We have no plans to introduce rent controls. International examples show they don’t necessarily bring rents down and our landmark Renters’ Rights Act already protects tenants from excessive rent increases. The Act limits rent rises to once a year, gives tenants strong powers to challenge above-market increases and bans rental bidding wars - giving renters the security they deserve.”

News.title: Watch: The life of an iconic country singer
News.content:
Iconic country musician Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80, her family announced on her social media.

"Sadness lies with us, not with Dolly," Parton's nephew Brian Seaver said in a video announcement.

In a seven-decade career, Parton won 10 Grammy awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote in excess of 3,000 songs.

Parton took her writing seriously, and considered herself a songwriter over everything else. "It's my way of expressing myself," she said. "It's my therapy."

She was also a savvy businesswoman who wasn't afraid to make tough decisions. Armed with a quick wit and southern charm, she took control of her show business career that spanned more than 60 years.

Follow for live updates and read more about Dolly's life.

News.title: Household energy bills to hit three-year high as Ofgem announces 4% rise from October
News.content:
Energy prices for millions of households will rise to the highest level for three years, under regulator Ofgem's price cap.

Ofgem said the price cap will increase by 4% on 1 October, driven by higher wholesale gas prices due to the Iran war.

A household using a typical amount of gas and electricity will pay Â£60 a year more, but more than a third of households are on fixed tariffs so their prices will not change.

The government said its cut to VAT on electricity bills will save households Â£45 and it was doing more to address cost of living pressures, but opposition parties said Labour was not doing enough.

The new cap will hit household bills as the colder weather arrives in October.

Suppliers say energy debt has rocketed and, with high bills likely to persist, have called for more support for those struggling to pay.

News.title: Dad of woman who took her own life says Treasury failed in its duty of care
News.content:
The father of a civil service employee who took her own life the day after a meeting with her managers has said the lack of support given to her by the Treasury "beggars belief".

Chloe Moffat, 26, a personal assistant to a Treasury director, died on 20 May last year, after she was told of allegations she had shared sensitive confidential information about colleagues, which she denied.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, David Moffat said he did not feel the Treasury had taken responsibility for its part in her death.

He added that her loss was "devastating", and had "torn such a big hole in our lives".

The Treasury said "it will learn the lessons from this tragedy".

On 19 May 2025, Chloe went to what she thought was a routine one-to-one with her line manager, but a more senior manager was also present.

"Chloe's first comment was, 'Oh, this must be serious, there's two of you here'", David told Today's Emma Barnett. "So that's the first time that she was aware of anything [that] might be a to do."

"And then they worked through and put several allegations to her that she'd shared confidential information."

During the meeting, David said she had asked on several occasions if she would lose her job, and if she could have a friend there - both of which were refused.

A coroner found at an inquest earlier in August that the Treasury did not apply written disciplinary policy, which would have made clear that if the allegations against Chloe were proven, the likely penalty was a written warning, not dismissal.

"Even though she asked, they said they could not determine the outcome," David said.

Straight after the meeting, Chloe was locked out of her emails. "That was all part of the shock and awe of it all for Chloe," David said.

The coroner found that the meeting between Chloe and her managers "materially contributed" to her death.

News.title: Yellow warnings remain in force as rain and thunderstorms hit parts of UK
News.content:
Downpours and thunderstorms will continue to bring the risk of flooding to parts of the UK on Wednesday.

A Met Office yellow warning for thunderstorms is valid until 22:00 BST, and was amended on Wednesday morning to cover northern and eastern Wales, as well as north-west England, the Midlands and parts of eastern and southern England.

The rain could be heavy enough to bring flash flooding and travel disruption, with lightning and large hail posing additional hazards.

Another Met Office yellow warning is in place for Thursday, when more thunderstorms are expected.

For some areas that have seen barely any rain so far this August, the next few days could bring the wettest weather in many weeks.

News.title: Why Pride is facing a backlash - from inside and outside the LGBT community
News.content:
Matt left Crewe as soon as he could, aged 18, feeling that he wasn't accepted as a young gay man. The only LGBT scene to mention was a tiny, makeshift bar behind a curtain in the back of an out-of-town pub.

He left in 2015, but this June found himself returning home, for Crewe Pride.

For Matt, it was a significant homecoming. "It really took me back to when I was a kid growing up here, trying to navigate my identity. It felt so important to be there and see how a town that wasn't particularly welcomingâ¦ has changed and flourished."

For many, these small, community Pride events feel a world away from the huge celebrations in the UK's largest cities.

But Matt's happy weekend in Crewe masks a growing culture war over Pride. Over the last few years, a number of councils have withdrawn their support for Pride festivals, while some big brands - perhaps nervous about being seen as too "woke" - have become hesitant to associate themselves with them. On top of all that, there's a long-running complaint from some LGBT campaigners that Pride has become overly commercialised; while the argument over trans issues has also made matters more fraught.

It's leading some to ask: what future do Pride events have?

News.title: Ex-England footballer Sterling charged with dangerous driving after crashing Lamborghini
News.content:
Raheem Sterling will appear in court next month to face charges of dangerous driving and possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation after crashing his car into motorway barriers in May.

The former England winger, who most recently played for Feyenoord in the Dutch Eredivisie, crashed his Lamborghini into barriers on the M3 in Hampshire on the morning of Thursday, 28 May.

The 31-year-old was arrested and then released on bail pending further enquiries.

A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman said: "A driver will appear in court next month to face charges following a collision on the M3.

"Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

"The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange [Hampshire], on 28 May, 2026.

"No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported. Mr Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court on 15 September."

Police suspected Sterling of "driving a vehicle whilst unfit through drugs," but that has not been included in the charges.

In May a source close to Sterling told BBC Sport there was "no proof" of drugs in his system.

The source added the player had faced "an extremely tough couple of years" and had been made to "feel worthless" and "forgotten about".

Sterling has been without a club since leaving Dutch side Feyenoord at the end of last season.

He joined Feyenoord in February on a short-term contract after leaving Chelsea by mutual consent.

Chelsea paid Â£47.5m to sign Sterling from Manchester City in 2022, where he had won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and one FA Cup in seven years.

In 2024 the former Liverpool winger joined Arsenal on loan, but upon returning to Chelsea in 2025 was exiled from the first-team squad and made to train separately.

Sterling earned 82 England caps between 2012 and 2022, and appeared at three World Cups and two European Championships.

News.title: NHS failing child sexual abuse victims in adulthood, say psychiatrists
News.content:
People sexually abused as children who seek help in later life for mental health problems are being failed by the NHS, senior doctors have told the BBC.

The Royal College of Psychiatrists is issuing a public apology for what it says is decades of mismanagement and misdiagnosis in the UK.

For some, it has worsened their traumas, it said.

The college said mental health staff have been too focussed on treating symptoms rather than exploring how past traumatic experiences can still affect patients.

Support is improving, it said, but there must be better training and more investment - something NHS bosses have said is being introduced.

The apology has been included in a report, external by the college and given to the BBC.

Immediate past president of the college, Dr Lade Smith, said she was "sorry" that, too often, victims have suffered "avoidable harm when seeking help".

The report details how treatment has sometimes been inappropriate, while people have been re-traumatised by the experience of repeated assessments and history-taking and not always being believed.

Dr Smith told the BBC it was clear people were not getting the support they needed, and that this was not just a failing of psychiatrists, but the whole mental health system.

"Services are so fragmented. The system is set up to provide short, discrete episodes of care. Psychiatrists do not get the time to build up a relationship with patients so they can be properly supported.

"They are lucky if they get eight sessions of therapy, when it could take eight sessions for a person just to disclose the abuse.

"And these are just the people who get support â many don't even get seen by mental health services because services are so stretched," she said.

News.title: Libyan who was cleared after Lockerbie bombing trial dies aged 70
News.content:
A Libyan who was cleared after standing trial over the Lockerbie bombing has died aged 70.

Al Amin Khalifah Fhimah was accused of murdering 270 people in the attack on Pan Am Flight 103 in December 1988.

He was found not guilty but a second Libyan, Abdulbasset Al Megrahi, was convicted of playing a key role in the bombing of the American airliner.

A Facebook post by Libyan Airlines announced Fhimah's death and expressed the company's condolences to his family.

Fhimah worked for the carrier in Malta before the bombing of Pan Am 103.

His funeral is set to take place on Wednesday in Tripoli, the capital of Libya.

News.title: Major Scottish gangland figure Steven Daniel arrested in organised crime raid
News.content:
One of Scotland's most high-profile gangland figures has been arrested during an early morning police raid.

Steven 'Bonzo' Daniel, 46 was taken into custody at around 06:00 from his home in Robroyston in the north of Glasgow.

Daniel is understood to be the head of the notorious Daniel crime family which has been engaged in a violent feud with the rival Lyons family for 25 years.

He was arrested in connection with serious and organised crime, firearms and drugs offences as part of Operation Ventetic, a major UK-wide operation which has dismantled several gangs.

News.title: Nicotine vapes best chance to quit smoking, major review finds
News.content:
Smokers who want to quit have the best chance of doing so if they use nicotine e-cigarettes, a review has found.

The Cochrane team looked at 80 major trials involving nearly 30,000 people and found that nicotine vapes were more effective than traditional aids such as patches, gum and support plans - increasing the success rate by about 60%, from around six in every 100 managing to quit smoking to one in every 10.

They outperformed non-nicotine vapes too, although researchers say switching to these afterwards might help with weaning off nicotine.

And they could prove more effective than the new anti-smoking pill cytisine, external, which the NHS has started to roll out - although more research is needed.

News.title: Father's house rammed before son died in A66 crash
News.content:
A house rammed by a car before the fatal A66 crash in Middlesbrough belonged to the father of a teenager who died in the incident.

Cole Worthy, 17, was one of five young men who died when a Volkswagen Passat travelling in the wrong direction hit a Cleveland Police armed response vehicle, also killing two police officers.

Before the crash at 03:39 BST on Saturday, police had received multiple reports of two cars driving dangerously around the town and a Volvo XC60 was seen ramming properties.

The BBC understands that, after his father's home was rammed, Worthy and the four others set out in the Passat. Police said they were linking the activities of the Volvo XC60 and the Passat.

There is no suggestion Worthy's father was involved in criminal activity.

PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, died in the crash, as did Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and Worthy.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct said officers had been pursuing the Passat for almost seven minutes after it was connected to earlier alleged criminal activity, but the pursuit was abandoned 10 seconds before the crash when it turned on to the dual carriageway.

Both vehicles were operating with cloned number plates but were picked up by automated number plate recognition technology.

News.title: Young care leavers dying early a 'national tragedy'
News.content:
Young adults who have left care have a death rate around four times higher than the general population, a new review, external shows.

Often left alone "with no safety net," the report says the consequences can be catastrophic.

On turning 18, people leaving care in England often lose "significant levers of support", the Government-commissioned report concluded, as it warned the so-called "care cliff" must be addressed.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4 Today, report co-author and broadcaster Ashley John-Baptiste, who grew up in care, called the deaths a national tragedy.

There were 112 deaths of care leavers aged 18 to 24 notified in 2025, which the review said equalled about 130 deaths per 100,000 care leavers.

John-Baptiste recalled his own experience of turning 18 and moving out of the last of four foster homes he'd lived in.

"I was made to live alone and work out how to be an adult," he said.

Unable to afford a bed frame, he says he slept on a mattress on the floor of his council flat and felt a deep sense of abandonment and isolation.

News.title: 'I'm still paying a mortgage for a home destroyed by a fire'
News.content:
Sarah Williams vividly remembers watching her home burn down on the news. On 26 August 2024, she was on holiday when a neighbour texted her to say the Spectrum Building in east London was on fire.

But two years on from the blaze in Dagenham, which left more than 80 people homeless, residents including Williams say they are still "in limbo".

The leaseholder said: "We're still just stuck waiting for other people to make decisions about our future."

She added that in a year's time, the money they were given through insurance to pay for alternative accommodation will run out, and she is still paying her mortgage for a home that does not exist.

At the time of the blaze, from which at least 20 people were rescued, work was under way to remove dangerous cladding. An investigation found the scaffolding around the building at the time had caused the fire to spread, although the exact cause of the blaze is unknown.

The government had provided almost Â£6m through its Building Safety fund to remediate the building - administered by the Greater London Authority (GLA) â with a clause stating that if the work was not completed, the money would have to be repaid.

The Spectrum Building was demolished in December 2024 after surveyor reports deemed it unsafe.

The building's freeholder, Arinium Ltd, has since gone into administration, leaving the administrators, FRP, in control of the company's assets, including the insurance proceeds.

The government says, external the GLA has told the building's administrators that the GLA may be owed money as part of the insolvency process.

The government says this is a standard procedural step and would not affect the money residents are owed, as the GLA would only receive any funds left after residents had been fully compensated.

The GLA said that, as is standard practice in insolvency law, it had informed the administrators of the government's interest as a potential creditor.

News.title: Calls for GPS monitoring of domestic abuse suspects after murder
News.content:
The campaign has been started by Lynne Mackenzie, herself a domestic abuse survivor, who lives a few miles from the isolated cottage where Stacy was killed in July.

Stacy's husband Jim Mair, 43, whose body was found beside her, had been charged with assaulting her but had reportedly been granted bail, external on condition that he did not approach her.

While Mackenzie did not know Stacy personally, she said she was shocked at her murder which happened just six days after the death of another domestic abuse victim, Vikki Soloman, in Edinburgh.

She told BBC Scotland News the killings led her to question whether enough was being done to protect women in Stacy's situation.

"Every time driving in and out of the village I was aware of the police at the end of the road," she said.

"And it really got me thinking what could we have done? What could have been put in place beforehand? What else do we need?"

She has been in contact with Stacy's family who have agreed for her name to be associated with the campaign.

News.title: 'We just want to get home' - dozens stranded in Tunisia after cancelled Belfast flight
News.content:
Dozens of people from Northern Ireland have been left stranded in Tunisia after their EasyJet flight home was cancelled, with the airline telling them it had no other flights available for another 10 days.

One man told BBC News NI he has spent Â£4,000 on travel home for his family-of-five, while another woman, Georgina Doherty, said she and her six children were trying to get home after the death of her mother-in-law.

Others described running out of medication for health issues, while EasyJet were also criticised over a lack of support and communication.

EasyJet has said it is operating an additional direct flight to Belfast on Tuesday night, and that it was "very sorry" for the inconvenience.

BBC News NI understands more than 100 people were booked onto the cancelled flight that was due to leave Enfidha-Hamamet Airport for Belfast International three days ago.

Stuart McCartney, from Dromore, County Down, said he had spent thousands on accommodation and flights to get his family home via a flight to Brussels.

"I'm willing to pay Â£4,000 to get us home, if needs be, and then battle for reimbursement if I have to after that," he said.

"But we shouldn't have to pay. My holiday was a fraction of what I'm paying to get home right now."

McCartney said EasyJet provided two nights of accommodation but then told the family to find alternative accommodation for the rest of the delay.

He said his mother Katherine, who accompanied his wife and children on the trip, relies on heart medication and they have had to keep a close eye on her remaining supply as the delay continued.

An EasyJet spokesperson said that the company "have been doing everything we can to support Mr McCartney, providing hotel accommodation and meals and we will be reimbursing expenses that may have been incurred".

Georgina Doherty, who is originally from Londonderry but now lives in County Donegal, told BBC News NI the last few days have been an "absolute nightmare" for her family.

Her husband returned home a day before they were due to fly back due to his mother taking ill. She has since died, with Doherty and her six children stranded in Tunisia.

News.title: Inspectors to assess police after Henry Nowak murder
News.content:
An inspection into how a police force responds to violent incidents has been launched in the wake of Henry Nowak's murder.

The 18-year-old student was stabbed in Southampton by Vickrum Digwa, who lied to police and insisted he had been the victim of a racist attack.

Hampshire Police officers initially arrested Nowak and placed him in handcuffs as he lay dying.

His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Service (HMICFRS) will assess the force's processes, training and how officers are supported to make sound and impartial judgements.

The inspection was requested by Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones, who said the public "must have confidence" in the force.

"This inspection will provide an independent assessment of the force's training, processes and culture, including the handling of allegations of racially aggravated assault," she said.

"Henry's family deserve answers, and the public deserve reassurance that their police service is equipped to recognise victims and provide the highest standard of care when it matters most."

Bangladesh is looking to buy Chinese J-10CE fighter jets and attack helicopters after being impressed by their performance in the four-day war between India and Pakistan.

Zahed Ur Rahman, an advisor to the prime minister, said on Tuesday that a government panel was preparing a draft purchase agreement to pitch to Beijing.

In addition to the fourth-generation multirole combat aircraft, the Bangladesh Air Force is seeking to buy VIP transport helicopters and unmanned aerial vehicle systems from China.

The defence procurement plan is aimed at modernising the air force and bolstering the country’s military muscle.

Speaking at a press conference, Mr Rahman said Dhaka had taken note of the strong performance of Chinese aircraft during a conflict in the neighbourhood.

He was referring to the brief May 2025 war that saw Chinese warplanes, including the J-10CE, flown by Pakistan get the better of the Indian Air Force. The Pakistan Air Force shot down multiple Indian warplanes with Chinese-made missiles fired from Chinese-made aircraft. India later acknowledged these losses, but did not clarify the number or nature of the downed aircraft.

A Bangladesh Air Force aerobatic display team performs during Victory Day celebrations in Dhaka ( AFP/Getty )

The aircraft for the Bangladesh Air Force would be acquired in the current fiscal year if funds were allocated in the budget, Mr Rahman said. If not, he added, the purchases would be done in the next budget cycle.

It wasn’t immediately clear how many aircraft Dhaka planned to take. Mr Rahman also didn’t disclose the value of the proposed deal or a delivery timeline, adding that such details would be determined in the course of negotiations with the Chinese side.

The draft acquisition agreement was prepared after preliminary negotiation meetings and sent to the Armed Forces Division and relevant ministries for formal review and administrative approval, he said.

Pakistan is so far the only ​confirmed foreign operator ​of the J-10CE, the ⁠export variant of the J-10C.

China has supplied naval vessels, ⁠combat ​aircraft, tanks, and missile systems to Bangladesh ​over the past two decades, making Beijing the largest source of ​military hardware for the South Asian nation.

Ukrainian commander Vladyslav Polskyi knew he had to do something when he saw two wounded fighters stranded on the battlefield — one of them still strapped to a land drone immobilized by a Russian strike.

A former science teacher who joined the army in 2023, the 29-year-old was watching the soldiers on a screen in his command post around 15 km away.

Between them stretched the "kill zone", riddled with mines and swarmed by aerial drones ready to attack anything that moved.

Polskyi, whose military call-sign is "Teacher", hopped into his grey pick-up truck and raced past scorched fields and the charred husks of other vehicles left on the battlefield of northern Ukraine. He had no helmet or body armour.

open image in gallery Ukrainian commander Vladyslav Polskyi, 29, receives the nation's highest military honour, the Hero of Ukraine, from Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiy ( Reuters )

"If it had happened to me, I would've wanted them to come take me away, and not just leave me there," the junior lieutenant told Reuters, recalling his August 15 mission to save both men, who were members of another battalion.

His feat captured the country's attention and earned him its highest military honour, Hero of Ukraine, days later. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy presented him with the award at Independence Day celebrations in Kyiv on Monday.

"People must be taken care of. Thank you, Vladyslav!" Zelenskiy said, announcing the award.

Stranded drone showed limits of battlefield tech

Speaking to Reuters less than a week after the operation, Polskyi described speeding toward the men while planning how he would load them onto the flatbed of the truck.

The two Ukrainian soldiers had been wounded during a combat mission in the Kharkiv region and were being evacuated atop an unmanned ground vehicle when it was struck by one of Russia's small, agile helicopter drones loaded with explosives.

open image in gallery Polskyi described speeding toward the men while planning how he would load them onto the flatbed of the truck ( Reuters )

Kyiv's forces have been using remote-controlled unmanned vehicles to help limit human involvement in dangerous tasks like evacuations inside the "kill zone", seeking an edge against Moscow's bigger army.

Russia's successful attack cast light on the limits of the relatively slow and rudimentary vehicles. The Russian drone knocked out the land drone's Starlink terminal, severing the link with its pilot and leaving it immobilized.

One of the wounded soldiers had managed to crawl into a ditch off the road and hide in the vegetation; the other lay helpless on the four-wheeled vehicle under an open sky, his right foot dangling from the bone.

Ukraine has also made widespread use of attack drones on the battlefield, and says it is killing or wounding around 30,000 Russian soldiers a month - a figure Moscow dismisses as exaggerated.

Both sides frequently post videos of drones hunting down each other's soldiers in the "kill zone".

Surveillance drone footage, obtained exclusively by Reuters from Polskyi's unit, the 475th Assault Regiment, shows his truck hurtling down a gravel road before turning and rapidly reversing toward the damaged drone.

open image in gallery Polskyi, 29 rescues injured service members from an unmanned ground vehicle ( Reuters )

Reuters was able to verify the exact location of the rescue using the full-length footage. However, the regiment asked not to disclose where it took place for security reasons.

At another nearby command post, drone-platoon leader "Malyi" watched as the rescue played out on screens in real time.

"Everyone in the command centre was shocked," said the 22-year-old, who asked to be identified by his call-sign. Just a single Russian drone or land mine could have killed all three men, he added.

Polskyi — dressed in T-shirt and shorts — hoisted both men onto his truck and raced home, managing to evade the flying Russian drones that had been detected heading toward their new target.

Looking back, he remembered the fear in the men's eyes. He was afraid too. "But you need to know how to control it," he said.
