Sports.title: Wolff 'not at all' disappointed by Verstappen's new Red Bull deal
Sports.content:
Mercedes chief Toto Wolff says he is "not at all" disappointed by Max Verstappen having committed to Red Bull with a new contract that runs until 2030.

Ahead of the Formula 1 season resuming with Verstappen's home Dutch Grand Prix over the weekend, Red Bull ended speculation over the four-time world champion's future by announcing the extension.

While Verstappen's previous deal was set to run until 2028, exit clauses in the agreement meant the 28-year-old would have been free to join another team in 2027, with possible switches to Mercedes and McLaren having been the subject of significant speculation.

Wolff made a very public pursuit of Verstappen after Lewis Hamilton announced in February 2024 that he was leaving Mercedes to join Ferrari in 2025, and the Mercedes boss appeared to still be interested in signing the Dutchman last season

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen admits that, with V8 engines' potential return in 2030, there may be another opportunity for him to reassess his future in F1

However, Wolff has insisted in recent months that he is happy with his driver pairing of Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, who sit first and second, respectively, at the top of the Drivers' Championship after Sunday's race in Zandvoort.

Asked about Verstappen's new contract in an interview with Sky Sports F1 on Saturday in Zandvoort, Wolff said: "Most important was that we had the clarity in the team since a long time.

"We're committed to George and Kimi, and in a way, that was just a logical consequence what happened now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff had previously downplayed suggestions Verstappen could join his team

"Silly season is officially cancelled now, and everybody can concentrate on the racing."

Pushed on whether he felt any disappointment about the length of Verstappen's commitment to Red Bull, Wolff added: "No, not at all.

"We know each other well. With Kimi and George, it's the perfect set-up we have and the perfect line-up, so there is no disappointment."

Rosberg: I don't think Max had any options

The cooling of Wolff's interest in Verstappen appears as though it may have been influenced by the hugely impressive form that has put Antonelli in control of the championship.

The Italian, who turned 20 on Tuesday, has unexpectedly outperformed the far more experienced Russell to build a 59-point advantage over his team-mate at the top of the standings.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix

While Mercedes showed huge faith in Antonelli by fast-tracking him in as Hamilton's replacement as a teenager, an inconsistent rookie campaign left doubt over whether he would be able to live up to expectations.

However, his 2026 form, which saw him break countless records by winning five successive races after finishing second in the season opener, could potentially have made Wolff reconsider whether bringing Verstappen to Mercedes remained necessary.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A 360-degree look at Verstappen’s race-ending crash at the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday

McLaren appeared to be similarly content with their current driver line-up of reigning world champion Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, who have combined to lead the Woking squad to successive constructors' titles.

Sky Sports F1 pundit Nico Rosberg, who won the 2016 world championship with Mercedes, said: "It's fantastic news for Formula 1 because Max Verstappen is the greatest driver at the moment, and we want him to stay here. He's a phenomenal driver!

"He was thinking about taking some time off, or stopping F1 for a while, so that's great.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico Rosberg discusses Verstappen's contract extension with Red Bull, saying it's a 'super important message' for the team

"I don't think he had any options. He was in talks with McLaren, but I think that was just to strengthen his position at Red Bull.

"Red Bull need stability so you offer him a bit more money, and the range is from £70-90m a year, so let's land on £80m - which is a lot of money!"

Sports.title: Serena and Alcaraz dazzle in mixed doubles before exit
Sports.content:
Star pairing Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reached the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed doubles before being beaten by fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.

Williams - a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion - returned to tennis in June at the age of 44 and secured her first professional win since 2022 as she and Alcaraz beat Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and partner Erin Routliffe in their opening match.

It was also seven-time major winner Alcaraz's first match back on tour after a wrist injury sidelined the reigning men's singles champion since April. The 22-year-old was born five years after Williams won the 1998 mixed doubles title at Flushing Meadows.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the US Open Mixed Doubles match between Serena Williams & Carlos Alcaraz vs Erin Routliffe & LLoyd Glasspool

The dynamic pairing bounced back from a slow start to claim a 5-3 4-1 opening victory over Routliffe and Glasspool, much to the delight of fans inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

"I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said. "I never thought this would happen."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carlos Alcaraz and Serena Williams react to Mixed Doubles US Open victory

With their quarter-final match scheduled immediately afterwards, Williams and Alcaraz ultimately ran out of puff as Bencic and Cobolli triumphed 5-4 4-1, the latter then having hailed their opponents pre-match as "the queen of tennis and the king of now."

The question now is whether Williams will seek an encore performance in women's doubles alongside older sister Venus, having already ruled out a repeat of her singles appearance at Wimbledon.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz won the first set of their Mixed Doubles match at the US Open

Djokovic and Sabalenka suffer early exit

Top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka were bounced out of the tournament in the opening match on Arthur Ashe, falling to a 1-4 4-2 10-2 ‌defeat to Britain's Henry Patten and Katerina Siniakova.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the US Open Mixed Doubles match between Aryna Sabalenka & Novak Djokovic vs Katerina Siniakova & Henry Patten

Djokovic, a ​24-time Grand Slam singles champion, and four-time major winner Sabalenka made a strong start by ​taking the opening set, but doubles specialists Patten and ‌Siniakova hit back to claim the second before dominating the tiebreak ​to secure a place in the quarter-finals.

Siniakova sealed the upset in style with an ace out wide on match ​point, ending the tournament hopes of the ⁠star-studded pairing.

"It wasn't looking very ⁠good for a while, in this format we play one bad game and all ‌of a sudden the first set's gone," Patten said.

"We knew the same could happen in the second, and we played ‌an amazing tiebreak. Kat acing Novak on match point was great."

The mixed doubles championship is once again being staged in the week before the singles main draw, after organisers revamped ⁠the format last year to attract more ​leading singles players by reducing the field and ​giving the event a standalone slot on the ​calendar.

The revamped format proved a commercial success in its ⁠debut year, drawing sell-out crowds and attracting many of the sport's biggest singles names despite criticism from some doubles specialists, ⁠who argued it marginalised established pairings.

Defending champions dumped out in first round

Italian ​duo Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori went on to ​retain the title by defeating Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud in last year's final, but suffered a first-round exit this year.

Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev beat the defending champions 1-4 4-1 11-9 in the opening round, before clinching a semi-final spot with a 4-1 4-5 10-5 victory over Diana Shnaider and Casper Ruud.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gael Monfils hit an incredible shot during his mixed doubles match at the US Open

They next face Czech pair Karolína Muchova and Jakub Mensik in one of Wednesday's semi-finals, with Bencic and Cobolli facing husband and wife partnership Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina in the other after they edged out Patten and Siniakova in the last eight.

The final two follow the two semis on Wednesday night will resemble a regular match, with traditional sets to six games.

Sports.title: Leeds earn second win at Forest in three days in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
Leeds United registered a second win at Nottingham Forest in three days as they booked their spot in the Carabao Cup third round.

Daniel Farke's side took the three Premier League points home on Saturday and earned a 2-0 victory in the League Cup thanks to goals from Dan James and James Justin.

Having not won at the City Ground since 1972 before the weekend, they have now triumphed there twice in 72 hours as the Yorkshire club enjoy a winning start to the new campaign.

It is not the start new Forest boss Oliver Glasner was looking for as things are yet to click, though additions are on the way with a £50m deal agreed for Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

Neither side will have been jumping for joy at the prospect of a rematch so soon after Saturday's Premier League opener.

But Forest enjoyed some early promise as James Trafford was forced into a great save in the 10th minute when he had to fend away Ola Aina's cross-shot, which almost left him wrongfooted.

Then Justin was in the right place at the right time to stop Igor Jesus' header from going in.

Leeds came into it and should have gone in front midway through the first half when James got in down the right, but his pull-back was just behind Sean Longstaff, who shot straight at Matz Sels.

Image: James Justin scores Leeds' second goal at Forest

Both sides were going for it and Leeds defender Joe Rodon denied Chris Wood with a brilliant last-ditch tackle while Sels kept out James' low effort at the other end.

The Wales international showed the required composure five minutes after the restart.

Aina's wayward header allowed Longstaff to gallop forward and he played in James, who clipped home.

Forest almost hit straight back as Arnaud Kalimuendo's cutback was perfect for Wood, but Trafford did brilliantly to stop his effort from going into the bottom corner, before Noah Okafor sent an effort just wide as Leeds staged a rapid counter-attack.

Leeds sealed the victory with 15 minutes remaining but there was nothing pretty about it.

Lucas Nmecha tried to claim it as his bundled effort was blocked on the line by Williams, with Justin finally putting the ball into the back of the net.

The managers...

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner told Sky Sports

"This is a little bit the assessment after six weeks here, that maybe - and not just in the team, it's maybe in the club - that there's a little bit of ignoring the reality.

"Right now, we are far away from where we want to be, and what I'm really convinced in that where we will be.

"The fact is that this team had a relegation battle for nine months. Very turbulent season and it ended with a huge effort to stay in the league, and this is our starting point.

"It's really very important not to blame anybody because sometimes I tell them facts and they say, 'Oh, Glasner is complaining'.

"No, no, no. But then maybe your best midfielder [Elliot Anderson] leaves the club and now we expect we compete for European places because Oliver Glasner is in. Sorry, this is what I can't deliver within six weeks.

"I'm no magician, no messiah, just hard work. That is what we have to do.

"It doesn't make sense talking about seventh two years ago. It's hard, it's tough, but if you ignore the reality then you live in dreamland and this is never the best thing to do."

Leeds boss Daniel Farke told Sky Sports:

"This is what we came for, and this was my main goal.

"You play a cup run to go through. Very happy with the level of the performance, because we had to wait very long for a win here at Nottingham and to do this two times within three days at such a tough ground, this remarkable level of performance was outstanding.

"Saturday was really a tight game, but today I think it's not in doubt that it was a fully deserved win."

Sports.title: All Blacks need late surge to avoid shock defeat to Lions
Sports.content:
New Zealand fought back from an 18-point ‌deficit in the second half to beat the Lions 41-35 and avoid a shock defeat at Ellis Park on Tuesday.

It means that the All Blacks have swept all four provincial teams to remain undefeated on their six-week, eight-match tour of South Africa, on top of beating the Springboks 33-16 in ​the first Test at the weekend.

New Zealand fielded only three players from that Saturday Test victory over South Africa on the same ground and involved five injury replacements summoned on tour - including one who arrived on Monday - as well as giving a debut to prop Saula Ma'u.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights as New Zealand scored five tries to beat South Africa 33-16 at Ellis Park and take a 1-0 lead in the four-Test series of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry

Their defence struggled and missed 19 tackles over the course of the contest that saw them trail 14-0 after seven minutes.

They were still behind at half-time and 35-17 behind in the 47th minute, as the Lions threatened to become the first South African provincial side to beat New Zealand since Orange Free State, now known as the Cheetahs, in 1976.

But like the Stormers, Sharks and Bulls who the All Blacks had already beaten, the Lions are out of season and not match fit.

Having not played since May 30 in the United Rugby Championship quarter-finals, New Zealand eventually came storming back in the last 30 minutes with four successive tries.

"The Lions came out hissing," Blackadder said. "But we stayed composed and found a way in the end. They were quality tonight."

Blackadder - whose father Todd was on the last traditional tour in 1996 - was one of the New Zealand standouts along with inside center Timoci Tavatavanawai, Narawa, and fly-half Richie Mo'unga, back from Japan and in a black jersey for the first time since the 2023 World Cup final.

All Blacks coach Dave Rennie thought Blackadder was phenomenal. "He's got a massive engine and was everywhere," he said.

Blackadder's Test prospects also improved after Anton Segner was ruled out of the rest of the tour.

Segner was a late withdrawal from the first Test reserves due to an ankle injury that's needed two surgeries. The injury was assessed as acute inflammatory arthritis and he won't be replaced in the squad.

Mo'unga, like New Zealand, got better as the game got older, but he and Beauden Barrett could convert only three of the team's seven tries.

On the other hand, Chris Smith, at home, converted all five of the Lions tries and hit the post with a long penalty.

Sports.title: Wilson scores on full debut as Brentford hit Birmingham for six
Sports.content:
Callum Wilson scored just six minutes into his full debut and captain Nathan Collins converted two headers as Brentford routed Championship side Birmingham 6-1.

The 34-year-old Wilson, who joined on a free transfer from relegated West Ham, seized his first opportunity with a crisp finish which took a deflection off defender Dael Fry, who had a debut to forget.

Brentford's Premier League quality was evident throughout and although Blues equalised through Demarai Gray just before the half-hour they were level for just seven minutes.

Image: Callum Wilson scored six minutes into his full Brentford debut

Lax defending saw Aaron Hickey and Collins score in quick succession to effectively seal the tie before half-time, with Mikkel Damsgaard getting on the end of a counter-attack to add the fourth.

Igor Thiago's smart close-range finish sent fans streaming for the exit, missing Collins' second header.

The Bees, quarter-finalists last season, had not beaten Birmingham in six previous meetings, the last a goalless draw more than five years ago in the Championship before they went on to bigger and better things which their ambitious hosts now hope to emulate.

Birmingham's priority remains promotion so, after opening with two league draws, boss Chris Davies made six changes, including goalkeeper Ryan Allsop, Fry and Argentinian striker Luis Vazquez.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Callum Wilson produced a composed finish to put Brentford ahead just six minutes into his first competitive start for the club.

However, the gulf to a Premier League squad was evident as Keith Andrews retained only three of the team which demolished Tottenham and saw three of his newcomers score and another, Yehor Yarmoliuk, run the midfield before he was forced off with injury.

Davies wants to meet the club's aspirations by playing their way out of the Championship but it proved their undoing before they had even had chance to get a foothold in the game as they fell foul of Brentford's high press at a short goal-kick.

Paik Seung-ho was slow to react to the loose ball and Yarmoliuk played in Wilson to fire home first-time from the edge of the area with the aid of a deflection.

But a miscontrol by Jannik Schuster saw the centre-back booked for bringing down Vazquez and from Paik's short free-kick Gray drilled a deflected shot through a crowd of players.

It was a brief moment of joy in an otherwise chastening night as a failure to deal with Vitaly Janelt's chip and Wilson's strength allowed Hickey to fire home an angled shot.

Collins jumped in front of Fry to nod in a simple header from Jaidon Anthony's cross but a ruthless Brentford went for the kill and, after bringing on the likes of Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Mamadou Sangare, scored three more after the break.

The managers...

Birmingham's Chris Davies:

"My message to supporters tonight is 'sorry'. It's not very pleasant and I can understand how frustrating it is for them.

"It was a very tough evening for us, a painful evening, and incredibly disappointing to lose a game 6-1 at home.

"There were many situations where we were just not good enough to compete and I take ultimate responsibility for it - and the players will have to do it in their own minds.

"We were beaten by a team a long way ahead of us in every aspect. Was 6-1 a fair reflection? Probably."

Brentford's Keith Andrews:

"I didn't really blink an eyelid making so many changes.

"There is a huge narrative around cup games with coaches making changes but with the squad we have, there are fine margins between who plays and doesn't play.

"We needed to compete really hard to play the game we wanted. I thought overall we produced a really good performance."

Sports.title: Martin O’Neill puts Champions League collapse among most painful Celtic nights
Sports.content:
Martin O’Neill has admitted Celtic’s Champions League qualifying collapse from 4-0 up ranks as one of his most painful nights as the club’s manager.

Celtic held a four-goal aggregate lead against Lask on Tuesday when Callum McGregor scored in the 21st minute in Austria, building on a 3-0 first-leg victory, and appeared to be cruising into the league stage. But they lost 5-1 on the night after extra time to go out in extraordinary fashion.

Defeat sends Celtic into the Europa League and delivers a damaging financial blow that will cost the club at least £20m. O’Neill has overseen more than 300 games as the club’s manager and said it was one of the most painful.

“I would say absolutely, yes,” the 74-year-old said. “I’d put it down before the disappointment of losing the Uefa Cup final in 2003, but it’s so, so disappointing.

“We should have been out of sight by half-time. We scored a goal, which was great, we missed two great, great opportunities. And then we give them a lifeline just before half-time and then one just after it. And they come roaring back.

“And obviously we conceded, from our viewpoint, not good goals at all. But that’s my team and that’s my responsibility.”

Asked whether his squad was strong enough, O’Neill said: “These are tough games. And it might only be a Champions League qualifying game, but it felt like a Champions League game. I thought they were a fine side. But that doesn’t matter. We should have been able to have seen it through. And we didn’t do. Talking about the squad, that’s for another day.”

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

McGregor, the captain, accepted there were no excuses. “We got what we deserved,” he told Amazon Prime. “I thought we were so passive. All night. We actually looked scared to go and win the game, and when you are 3-0 up it’s psychological.

“To be honest I didn’t think we were that good in the first leg either. We scored at good times and kind of got away with it. You go 3-0 and you think you’ve got a real chance but when you play like that you can’t have any excuse whatsoever.

“We have to suck it up, apologise to the supporters and the club because there is no way that we should lose that game … Now you’ll see what kind of characters are in there.”

Sports.title: De Zerbi hopes Sávio’s fresh start will help Spurs’ much-needed rebrand
Sports.content:
What’s in a name? Quite a bit, judging by the discussion at Roberto De Zerbi’s Tottenham press conference on Tuesday, shortly after the club had completed the £75m signing of Savinho from Manchester City and the Brazil winger had let everybody know that he wanted to be called Sávio from now on. He will have that name on his Spurs shirt above his No 17, which he has taken over from Cristian Romero, the former captain who has moved to Atlético Madrid.

The 22-year-old went by Sávio at various times before his two seasons at City but there was nonetheless speculation about the reasons for the reversion. Savinho translates roughly from the Portuguese as “little Sávio”. Was it him saying that he was now an older and more mature player?

On the subject of theories, there is one about the fee, which could rise to £85m in add-ons. Even at £75m, it represents a record sale for City, who paid £30.8m to take Sávio from Troyes. Spurs are pushing to sign another attacker from City – Omar Marmoush, whose previous club Eintracht Frankfurt have a sell-on clause. Are Spurs paying more for Sávio in order to pay potentially less to City for Marmoush, which could reduce the liabilities to Eintracht?

De Zerbi has plenty on his plate after Spurs’ dismal 3-0 defeat at Brentford on Saturday in their Premier League opener and before the Carabao Cup tie at home against Charlton on Wednesday night.

“Listen, I lost 3-0 in the first game in the Premier League … do you think for me it’s a problem if Savinho becomes Sávio?” he said, turning to face his interpreter. “If Enrico [the interpreter] becomes Savinho, it’s a problem. If Savinho stays Sávio, nothing changes for me.”

De Zerbi said the talks for Sávio had started three days after the end of last season. It has been a mini‑epic to get the deal over the line but well worth it, according to the Spurs manager, who rates Sávio as one of the best in the world for being able to get past his marker when one‑against‑one. The challenge for Sávio will be to improve his end product, particularly in terms of goals. He scored only seven for City in all competitions and only two in 53 Premier League appearances. Sávio is available for selection against Charlton, his paperwork having been completed in time.

De Zerbi did get around to accepting that Sávio’s rebrand was part of a fresh start for the player. What is not in doubt is Spurs’ need for one after Brentford, when all the excitement around a summer of heavy spending turned to frustration; a very familiar sinking feeling.

View image in fullscreen New Tottenham signings Jan Paul van Hecke (left) and Sandro Tonali (right) after Spurs conceded their second goal during their 3-0 defeat at Brentford. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

It is possible to explain away the shambles against Brentford, who were not only much more joined-up but appeared to want it more in the duels. De Zerbi has attempted to do so in that way beloved of managers, emphasising he is not making excuses, you understand, just stating facts.

He had a completely new back four compared with his preferred unit from the end of last season; a new midfield pair, too. Up front from right to left, Mikey Moore, Richarlison and Mathys Tel were nobody’s idea of a trio to drive the push for Champions League football. De Zerbi was missing a host of players because of fitness issues, including Pedro Porro, Micky van de Ven, Mateus Fernandes and Dominic Solanke. Some of the issues can be traced to the slog of a pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia, which De Zerbi continues to reference in irritated tones.

These facts do not really wash. The performance against Brentford was unacceptable. There is the sense that it will work out for Spurs, mainly because they have De Zerbi and a collection of Premier League‑ready new signings. They have certainly put themselves under pressure for the visit of Charlton. A relevant statistic: Spurs have won one domestic home game in 2026 – against Everton on the final day of last season which enabled them to avoid relegation.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

De Zerbi made the point that he and the squad had “started the project right now, not last season”. Which was when he was parachuted in with seven games to go; he picked up 11 points to dodge the unthinkable. “Last season, we fought to stay up,” he said. The inference was that it would take rather more to become a proper team.

On the other hand, the experiences of the previous campaign do offer reassurance. “Maybe last season was a tougher challenge to stay up than this season,” De Zerbi said. “I said to the players: last season, in a worse situation, we showed character, we showed balls. We showed pride and quality. Now we have to stay calm and to analyse better the situation – not to have an emotional reaction. We have to be intelligent.”

What De Zerbi craves is consistency, which he defined as being five wins in a row. It seems a distant goal after Brentford but De Zerbi has faith. What it will take is a change to the collective mentality. “We have to get used to winning games and games and games – we have to change habits from the last two seasons,” he said.

“For me, the Carabao Cup is like the Premier League. We are not in the condition to make differences [between the competitions]. We have to play well and get used to winning – and winning matches, not a match. We have to change the mood. And we can.”

De Zerbi said that Porro and Van de Ven will return as substitutes against Charlton and Solanke may start. James Maddison is out for two weeks with a shoulder injury suffered against Brentford. De Zerbi has a decision to make on Sávio. Victory is non-negotiable.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession
Sports.content:
The former England forward Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway, police have said.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight constabulary said the charges followed a single-vehicle collision on the M3 southbound, near Minley interchange, on 28 May. The 31-year-old is accused of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.

The force said that no other vehicles were involved in the collision and no injuries were reported. Sterling, from Berkshire, is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court for a hearing on 15 September.

Quick Guide How do I 

He scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020. Sterling came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut, and moved in 2015 to Manchester City, with whom he won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but after falling out of favour spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal. After leaving Stamford Bridge, Sterling joined the Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of last season. He is without a club.

In the 2021 Queen’s birthday honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out strongly against racism on and off the pitch.

Sports.title: After Dom Ballard’s backheel, what is the earliest goal of the season? | The Knowledge
Sports.content:
“After watching Dom Ballard’s backheel volley for Bristol City against Birmingham in game week two of the Championship, it begs the question: what’s the earliest in a season a goal has gone on to win goal of the season?” asks Ricardio Sentulio.

There is no doubting Dom Ballard’s outrageous flick for Bristol City at Birmingham City should be a Puskás contender, especially with his finish kissing the crossbar on its way in, and has a very good chance of being the best goal scored in the 2026-27 Championship season, even though there is a long way to go.

Ballard’s wondergoal was scored on 22 August, on gameweek two. Eleven years ago to that day, Marco Matias notched this ridiculous effort for Sheffield Wednesday at Leeds United, although it should be said that Yorkshire derby was gameweek four, so technically later in the 2015-16 season than Ballard’s. Matias was given the goal of the season gong in April 2016.

The earliest Championship goal of the season we could find was the 2022-23 effort from Ismaïla Sarr for Watford. The Senegalese, now at Palace, scored from the halfway line to stun West Brom on the opening day (8 August). It doesn’t get much earlier, especially as Sarr’s strike was just 12 minutes into the match.

David Beckham’s famous goal for Manchester United against Wimbledon in 1996-97, lobbing Neil Sullivan from the halfway line – later voted the best of that Premier League campaign – was also on the opening day of the league season but came later in the year (11 days after Sarr) and also in the 87th minute (so 75 minutes later than Sarr in the match).

View image in fullscreen A 21-year-old David Beckham, there, on his way to superstardom. Photograph: Tony O’Brien/Action Images/Reuters

In Scotland, the 2017-18 SPFA goal of the season was given to Kieran Tierney for Celtic versus Kilmarnock, also on 8 August (2017) in the League Cup. Even though that is the same date as Sarr’s strike, the cup tie actually came three days after Celtic’s opening league game, a 4-1 win over Hearts on 5 August 2017. We could also mention that Celtic’s Jota once scored a goal of the month (for August even though the goal was in July) for Celtic against Aberdeen (31 July 2022, game one).

We finish with a goal that probably doesn’t quite fit into this category but is too good to ignore or forget. Schalke’s goal of the year (not season, it should be stated) in 2013 came as early as on 27 July but comes with three caveats: a) it was in a pre-season friendly; b) it was by a player that wasn’t even on Schalke’s books at the time of scoring; and c) it was a tap-in.

After two successful years at Schalke, Raúl had joined Al-Sadd, with a pre-season friendly arranged as part of the deal. So when Al-Sadd travelled to Gelsenkirchen on 27 July 2013, Raúl agreed to play the first half for his new side and the second half for Schalke. The Spaniard scored twice for the latter, the first of which was a textbook right-place-right-time finish from two yards out. To understand why it was voted Schalke’s goal of the year, you are going to have to check out the assist from a teenage Julian Draxler.

Have you any earlier examples from further afield? Mail us with your questions and answers.

Spinning plates

“Has a club’s player-manager ever been called up for an international cap, or travelled to play during an international break in the club season?” asks Frederick Sondheimer-Acosta.

Let’s start with a couple of famous examples from the Scotland team of the mid-1980s. “Kenny Dalglish became Liverpool player-manager in the summer of 1985 and subsequently played a few games for Scotland, including the first leg of their World Cup playoff win against Australia,” writes Dom Miller. “He won his 100th cap against Romania in March 1986 and was initially selected for the World Cup squad but withdrew due to a knee injury picked up in the FA Cup final (there has always been a suspicion he didn’t go because his mate Alan Hansen wasn’t picked). Dalglish won his last two caps in the autumn of 1986.”

View image in fullscreen Player-manager Kenny Dalglish (top right) and Liverpool celebrate winning the 1985-86 First Division at Stamford Bridge. Dalglish scored the winning goal to beat Chelsea and clinch the title. Photograph: David Cannon/Getty Images

Scotland, with Alex Ferguson in temporary charge after the tragic death of Jock Stein, did have a player-manager in their squad for the World Cup. Graeme Souness was appointed by Rangers in April and played the first two games at Mexico 86, when Scotland were a little unfortunate to lose to Denmark and West Germany. But Souness struggled with the altitude, saying he never felt worse on a football field than during the West Germany game, and Ferguson left him out of their final group match against Uruguay.

Another mighty, all-purpose midfielder, Johnny Giles, went one better than Souness. “Perhaps uniquely, Giles held player-manager positions for club and country simultaneously,” writes Bruce Mair. “He was player-manager of the Republic of Ireland, a part-time post, from May 1973 until March 1980 while playing for Leeds United (1973-75) and serving as player-manager of both West Bromwich Albion (1975-77) and Shamrock Rovers (1977-80). Giles selected himself for 24 of his 59 international appearances.”

Those are the most high-profile examples in Britain and Ireland, but there are dozens more cases – thanks to Bruce Mair, in particular, for doing so much work on this. We’ve picked some of the more interesting examples:

Andy Aitken “The earliest player-manager I can find,” writes Bruce. “Won three caps for Scotland while player-manager of Middlesbrough, 1907-08, and three more when player-manager/secretary at Leicester Fosse (now Leicester City), 1910-11.

Orvar Bergmark “Played 41 internationals for Sweden, including their run to the 1958 World Cup final, while player‑manager of Örebro between 1958 and 1961.”

Gunnar Gren “Seventeen caps for Sweden while player-manager of Örgryte IS, 1957-58. A teammate of Orvar Bergmark in the Swedish side that reached the 1958 World Cup final.”

Stuart Pearce “Capped twice for England in 1997 during his stint as caretaker player-manager at Nottingham Forest.”

Fanny Vágó “Hungary’s most‑capped women’s international made 19 appearances for her country while player‑manager of Ferencvárosi TC between 2021 and 2023.”

Elisha Scott “Liverpool legend won four caps for Northern Ireland while player-manager of Belfast Celtic at the tail end of his career, 1934-36.”

John Toshack “Six appearances for Wales as Swansea City player-manager in 1979.”

Jim Platt “Played twice for Northern Ireland in 1984 as player-manager of Ballymena United and made one further appearance as player-manager of Coleraine in 1986. Member of Northern Ireland’s 1986 World Cup squad.”

Knowledge archive

“Has there ever been an occasion where a major team has been disrupted by jury service, with either a manager or a player being called up during the season?” James Schofield asked back in May 2018.

“Plymouth’s Welsh international Carl Fletcher once tried to argue he couldn’t sit on a jury as he was too well known,” answered Andy Carswell. “According to reports in 2010, Judge Francis Gilbert told the midfielder that being Plymouth captain was not sufficient reason to excuse him, and that he had enough time to travel to Cheltenham for a Johnstone’s Paint Trophy tie after completing his duties. Fletcher argued that his position meant he was in a position of potentially being threatened, saying: ‘I don’t want anything to come back on me for sitting on a jury.’ His protests fell on deaf ears, with Judge Gilbert adding: ‘Lots of well-known people, some more famous than you, have been required to sit on juries.’”

James Perch had just helped Newcastle United to fifth place in 2012 but was also forced to cut short a holiday to Dubai after learning of his higher calling. “I’ve got jury service, unless I can be excused,” he told the club website. “It’s killed my holiday a bit, but at the minute I’m set to be in court at the end of May.”

Can you help?

“As someone who occasionally has to search for football stadiums to find directions and the like, I always enjoy that people take the time to rate their experience of visiting a football ground,” begins our own Will Unwin. “Hull City, for example, have 4.3 stars from 3,655 reviews. I therefore ponder … which ground has the highest and lowest Google rating?”

“I was surprised, staggered in fact, to see Nottingham Forest as the 18th team in the Guardian season previews,” writes Ross Connett. “I associate 18th place with the likes of Tottenham or West Ham, never a team beginning with N, just scraping over halfway into the alphabet. Has there ever been a more ‘early alphabet team’-dominated Premier League?”

“During Fulham v Chelsea, the previous jobs of both the opposing managers was coincidentally at the same club, Real Madrid,” notes Sarang Satish. “Are there other times this has happened?”

“Who has scored the highest percentage of their professional goals in hat-tricks?” asks Michael D.

“Last weekend every match in the Gibraltar league was a draw,” mails Stephen Hogg. “There are very few teams in the league, however. What’s the biggest league where this has happened?”

“This season Istanbul has six clubs in the Turkish top flight,” starts Vasco Wackrill. “What is the record number of top-flight clubs supplied in a season by a non-capital city?”

“Three of Kevin Lisbie’s sons are playing professionally; in the Championship (Kyrell, Millwall), in League One (Kyreece, Reading) and League Two (Kaion, Colchester United),” writes Stuart Willsher. “Have we ever had four brothers playing in all four top English divisions?”

Sports.title: Victor Torp seals Coventry’s Carabao Cup win at Plymouth in six-goal thriller
Sports.content:
A midweek jaunt to Devon always had the makings of a tricky trip for a Coventry team focused on Premier League survival. Such feelings quickly evaporated when Frank Lampard’s side raced into a two-goal lead with just four minutes and six seconds on the clock, Taiwo Awoniyi opening his account for his new club before Jack Rudoni doubled Coventry’s advantage. But, ultimately, Coventry were made to toil before chalking up a welcome first victory of the season.

Plymouth have form for a cup upset and another was brewing when Xavier Amaechi pulled Tom Cleverley’s side level nine minutes into the second half. Coventry, to their credit, roused once more, the substitute Ephron Mason-Clark regaining the lead before Victor Torp sealed progress to the Carabao Cup third round from the penalty spot. “You’ve got to enjoy a win, always,” Lampard said. “A win is a big deal because it’s a nice feeling to take back on the bus for four hours.”

The 2,244 Coventry supporters, many of whom made the 444-mile round trip, cycled through the catalogue of songs after crisp finishes by Awoniyi and Rudoni. Then Lampard obliged when they craved a wave from a manager who led them back to the top flight after 25 years away. But the game did not turn into the non-event most would have envisaged. “It’s very easy to go: ‘Why don’t you just go 2-0 up and then beat Plymouth 5-0, 6-0?’” Lampard said. “I’ve played in these games many times with different teams and they can become awkward, especially when the flow of the game goes against you: the crowd turns, emotions catch up and all of a sudden the game feels very different. I thought we dealt OK with that, in the end.”

Plymouth were suddenly liberated at 2-0 down. The Danish centre-back Mathias Ross sent a header wide from a free-kick and a couple of minutes later Oliver Irow read Harvey White’s flighted pass and the Tottenham loanee, 24 hours after signing, drove inside Joel Latibeaudiere and drilled past the Coventry goalkeeper Dan Bentley, another debutant. From there, aside from Awoniyi heading wide unmarked, Coventry had to withstand Plymouth pressure. After fumbling White’s shot from distance, Bentley diverted Will Evans’s rebound on to his left post.

Cleverley knew the value of recording an upset, Lampard the damage of defeat. It must have crossed his mind when Amaechi levelled on 54 minutes. Amaechi swarmed Liam Kitching and pinched the ball after the Coventry defender got in a tangle and fired in. Plymouth introduced the homegrown academy graduates Tegan Finn and Caleb Roberts, joining the 17-year-old full-back Joe Mwaro, this his full debut, on the pitch. “I couldn’t be happier with the reaction and the quality we showed to make sure it was still a competitive game,” Cleverley said.

View image in fullscreen Jack Rudoni doubles Coventry’s lead from close range in the fifth minute. Photograph: Dan Mullan/Getty Images

Mason-Clark arrived for his first appearance of the season after a hamstring issue and added the fifth goal of an entertaining game. It was a galling goal from a Plymouth perspective. Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s cross from the right caused problems, Mason-Clark at first failing to divert the ball goalwards. But Torp was alert to the ball dropping at the back post and squared to provide Mason-Clark the simplest of finishes, the forward poking in from inside the six-yard box.

Lampard made a triple sub, Sidiki Cherif replacing Awoniyi for his debut, while Josh Eccles and Brandon Thomas-Asante also entered. Joe Edwards, the Plymouth midfielder, arrived from the bench but his first notable action was to inadvertently swipe at Thomas-Asante in the box when trying to clear the leftovers of a Coventry corner, giving the referee, Elliott Swallow, no choice but to award a penalty. Torp capped the scoring, thrashing the spot-kick into the top corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

For Cleverley, this also represented a touchline duel with a friend and a former England teammate and he had spoken on the eve of the game of wanting English coaches like Lampard and Michael Carrick, another former teammate, to succeed. “If you do well in it, you’re great for a moment, if you don’t do so well, then you’re not,” Lampard said after. “If you have the English tag, I do think we’ve got a bit of a bracket of saying: ‘There’s another one [struggling].’ Hopefully we’re not idiots and we can show that over a period of time and do our jobs well.”

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Jean-Philippe Mateta to Aston Villa?
Sports.content:
Liam Delap may not have broken any records during his time with Chelsea but he is setting one on his way out the door. The England youth international is thought to be breaking Nottingham Forest’s transfer fee record with Oliver Glasner bringing him in for an expected £50m. The fee comes despite a disappointing 2025-26 season with the 23-year-old striker scoring only one Premier League goal.

Injury problems with his shoulder and hamstring did not help but the lack of return means the Blues were open to selling the striker and Forest have taken the bait. If Delap does sell for £50m it also means Chelsea will make a £20m profit on the player after buying him from Ipswich for £30m in 2025.

Delap isn’t the last deal Forest want to get over the line before Monday’s deadline day either as they are interested in Corinthians and Brazil midfielder André.

One story that is gathering momentum like a ball in snow is Jean-Philippe Mateta moving to Aston Villa. The Villans have made Crystal Palace an offer for the France striker but it is a long way off what the London club would like.

A departure that could finance Mateta’s move could be that of Ollie Watkins, though it is one that has shocked Villa. It has been extensively reported the English international has interest from Saudi club Al-Hilal with his signature set to be worth about £59.8m. Villa are close to agreeing the move and it is understood Watkins would have an annual salary of £12m.

With deadline day approaching, last-minute signings will come out of the woodwork at every turn. Let’s rattle through some. Manchester United are interested in Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch, Newcastle have submitted a bid for Lille winger Matias Fernandez-Pardo, West Ham defender El Hadji Malick Diouf may play in the Premier League again with Brentford close to a deal for the Senegalese player, newly promoted Hull have agreed a move to sign Ilyas Ansah from Union Berlin in a deal worth £20m and Tottenham are pushing to sign Omar Marmoush from Manchester City.

If Spurs did get that move over the line for the Egypt forward then the club’s spend this summer would be close to £400m. It is no wonder fans looked lost for words at Tottenham’s 3-0 loss to Brentford last weekend.

We started with Chelsea so let’s end with the Blues. Enzo Fernández, who was met with a wall of boos when Chelsea played Fulham in their opening fixture, may not play in London for much longer. Manchester City will submit a bid for the Argentina midfielder before deadline day. If they do, it could be the biggest transfer of the summer so far with Chelsea reportedly wanting £120m for the 25-year-old.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

So Fernández may travel up the M1 and M6 but the boos are likely to follow him after he scored and showboated in England’s defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 5: Charlton Athletic
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 14th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 3rd (WSL2)

Prospects

Just under 20 years since Charlton’s successful women’s team were disbanded after the men’s team’s relegation from the Premier League, they are finally back in the limelight and ready to make a name for themselves again.

Karen Hills’s side impressed for much of last season, going on a 27-game unbeaten streak and possessing the meanest defence in WSL 2. A mid-season blip harmed their race for the title, however, and they lost out to Birmingham City on the final day of the season, ultimately going through a playoff to achieve their goal of promotion. Beating Leicester in that game will have given Hills and her players confidence that they can compete. There will be no complacency, however, having seen how newly promoted sides have fared in recent history.

Six players have departed since last season, including the influential Katie Bradley But they have been replaced with a blend of knowhow and exciting young talent. The arrival of Ashleigh Neville and Emily van Egmond will bring experience to Hills’s dressing room. Leah Davidson’s and Grace Johnston’s arrivals from Australia are intriguing moves. Meanwhile, Sophie Whitehouse was the hero of the previous campaign and Charlton will be looking to the goalkeeper to again lead from the back. It is the attacking side of the game that perhaps causes the most concern. Charlton managed only 31 goals last season, the lowest of the WSL2’s top six.

Preparations got under way with a pre-season trip to Cádiz, a chance for a new-look side to come together. There is no doubt that the task to stay up is a challenging one, but a club that have defied the odds on more than one occasion will believe they can do it again.

Off-field picture

A record-breaking partnership has seen haircare brand Sofnfree become the women’s team’s official sleeve partner. The branding will feature on all playing and replica shirts this season, while content creation will be a focus as Charlton hope to access new and existing audiences. The club have also launched their first women’s-centric TikTok channel. The news, however, that ownership group Global Football Partners have put the club up for sale could cause a bit of instability in the short term.

The manager

Reaching the Women’s Super League was part of the five-year plan Hills had when she was appointed in 2021, bringing a club close to her heart back into the limelight. The 51-year-old represented Chartlon for six years as a player, winning the FA Cup in 2005. This is the second time in Hills’s coaching career she has guided a team to the top flight, having previously done so with Tottenham in 2019, and watching Charlton walk out at the Valley against Liverpool on 6 September will inevitably be an emotional moment for her.

View image in fullscreen Karen Hills has guided a club into the top flight for the second time after have done so with Spurs in 2019. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Alamy

Star signing

Only three months ago, Neville was lining up against Charlton in the promotion playoff. Now she is a fully fledged Addick, joining from Leicester on a two-year deal. The full-back brings with her a wealth of experience having made more than a century of appearances in the WSL. The majority of those were under Hills at Tottenham after arriving there from Coventry United. A tough-tackling, intuitive defender, Neville never shirks a challenge and has the ability to push forward. She will also be a strong leader in the dressing room.

Stat attack

Despite finishing third in WSL2, Charlton kept the joint-most clean sheets and conceded the fewest goals in the division. No club saved as high a percentage of their shots on target faced, with Whitehouse playing every minute. She saved four penalties in the playoff shootout, too.

Set for a breakthrough

Johnston was named Charlton’s first signing of the summer during a transfer window that has seen many A-League players depart for Europe. The versatile young full-back arrives at the Valley hoping to make her mark on English football after three seasons with Perth Glory. She impressed during her time with her home town club, played every minute of last season, winning the club’s 2026 best young player award. Johnston’s form led to her being called up to the Young Matildas in 2023, representing the under-20s and now the under-23s. She was an integral member of the squad that won the Asean Women’s Championship last year.

What they say …

“I know what Karen’s about and vice versa; she knows what I bring. I’m really looking forward to working with her again” – Ashleigh Neville

Where are they playing their home games?

Charlton will play their home games at the Valley for a third consecutive season. Season-ticket sales started almost immediately after their successful promotion push. Alcohol will also still be allowed in the stadium, with an alcohol-free section established. Other fan activations include giving supporters the opportunity to sponsor a player.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes and Khadija Shaw land PFA Player of the Year awards
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned Professional Footballers’ Association Player of the Year as Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw won the women’s award for the second time.

Playmaker Fernandes broke the record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcome a shaky first half of the campaign to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick to earn a Champions League return.

Fernandes was pleased to have been voted the winner by his fellow professionals. He said: “It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it’s probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment.”

The Portugal international is the club’s first winner since Wayne Rooney took home the trophy in 2009-10, and adds to his Football Writers’ Association Footballer of the Year award from May.

Shaw, who was also recognised by the FWA, scooped the PFA Women’s Player of the Year award for the second time. The 29-year-old claimed the trophy in 2023-24 and won it again having scored 21 goals on the way to a third consecutive Golden Boot and her maiden Women’s Super League title.

Arsenal’s Olivia Smith picked up the women’s PFA Young Player of the Year title for the second campaign running, having won the 2025 crown for her exploits at Liverpool before continuing her form in the capital.

Manchester City’s Nico O’Reilly was named men’s PFA Young Player of the Year following an outstanding campaign that ended with the versatile talent helping England to win World Cup bronze. The 21-year-old was part of the PFA Premier League Team of the Year along with City teammates Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo.

O’Reilly said: “I had a great season. I’m very proud of the season I had. I won two trophies with my club and managed to play at the World Cup with my country. I’m over the moon how it turned out.”

Champions Arsenal had five representatives in David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurriën Timber and Declan Rice, with Player of the Year Fernandes of United and Brentford’s Igor Thiago completing the team.

The PFA WSL Team of the Year featured three players from triumphant City, with Shaw joined by teammates Kerstin Casparij and Yui Hasegawa.

Mariona Caldentey, last year’s PFA Women’s Player of the Year, was joined in the XI by fellow Arsenal players Emily Fox and Alessia Russo. Tottenham defender Toko Koga and Manchester United’s Jess Park were also included in the team, as were the Chelsea trio of Hannah Hampton, Ellie Carpenter and Lauren James.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Hayden Hackney, now of Everton, was named Championship PFA Players’ Player of the Year for his performances for defeated play-off finalists Middlesbrough.

Dom Ballard, who scored a jaw-dropping effort for new club Bristol City at the weekend, collected the League One award for a goal-laden season at Leyton Orient.

Swindon striker Aaron Drinan’s performances saw him collect the League Two award, while Lily Crosthwaite of Birmingham took the WSL2 player accolade.

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney received the PFA merit awards in recognition of their contribution to football. Dalglish enjoyed a success-laden career as a player with Celtic and Liverpool, and is Scotland’s most capped performer having represented his country on 102 occasions. The 75-year-old, who confirmed in June he was undergoing treatment for cancer, went on to enjoy a successful managerial career, leading Liverpool to three league titles before masterminding Blackburn’s Premier League triumph.

Carney played 144 times for England, including being part of the Lionesses squad which finished third at the 2015 World Cup. Having come through the ranks at Birmingham, Carney won the quadruple with Arsenal in 2007 as well as a league and FA Cup double with Chelsea in 2018.

Sports.title: ‘Murder’ – Alan Brazil reveals night from hell immediately after Celtic horror show
Sports.content:
Alan Brazil endured the night from hell after watching Celtic crash out of the Champions League - before arriving late to work.

The talkSPORT co-host has been left in disbelief by the Hoops' 5-4 play-off defeat on aggregate to Austrian outfit LASK.

4 Celtic will be playing Europa League football after failing to qualify for the Champions League Credit: Getty

Martin O'Neill's side led 3-0 on aggregate having eased to victory last week in Glasgow, and they got off to the perfect start on Tuesday night after Callum McGregor's 23rd minute opener.

But they somehow blew a four-goal lead, with LASK taking the game to extra-time before scoring a winner through Samuel Adeniran's 109th minute long range effort.

It means that Celtic have now crashed out in the Champions League play-offs for a second successive season, with the Scottish giants set for another campaign of Europa League football.

If that wasn't bad enough for Brazil, he then struggled to get to sleep, leading him to head down to London from Ipswich early in the night.

Meanwhile, problems on the road led to him getting an even later night's sleep in the capital - leaving Rangers icon Ally McCoist to be on solo presenting duties on the Sports Breakfast show.

Why was Alan Brazil late for work?

With Brazil not in the talkSPORT studio McCoist quipped: "So the question is this, is Brazil late this morning after Celtic's embarrassment?"

Brazil would eventually arrive a few minutes later, where he would discuss his night from hell.

After a cheerful McCoist asked his colleague, 'How are you pal?,' the ex-Manchester United forward simply replied: "Murder."

Keen to get an excuse out of Brazil, McCoist then said: "Traffic? Tired? Slept in? Just depressed?"

To which Brazil remarked: "I'm not depressed, I'm not depressed, I cannot sleep."

4 Celtic boss O'Neill watched his side capitulate in real time against LASK Credit: Getty

He continued: "I was in Ipswich, at 11 o'clock [pm] I thought, 'This is ridiculous,' I went to bed at 7 [pm], could not sleep.

"I've got this... it's a long story... sciatica as well I've got... and then at 11 o'clock I said, 'Right, I'm going.'

"She [Jill Brazil, Alan's wife], didn't know [I left], so she's gone crazy this morning, woke up, 'Where am I?'

Brazil added: "And then coming into London, ahh, road shut, anyway, I got here, straight to bed, could not sleep.

"Up at 2 [am], 3 [am] and then I popped two aspirin plus or something - I suddenly woke up at 5.40 [am], I went, ' 'Ahh no!'"

He then proceeded to discuss Celtic's horror performance, remarking: "I said after the first game it's not over, but then when Celtic scored, I thought, 'Well that's it surely.'

4 Celtic have now failed to reach the Champions League group stage in the last two seasons Credit: Getty

"Unbelievable, it's unbelievable, the punters were going crazy at the board again, terrible.

"When McGregor scores, you think, 'Well, that's it, just lock up, keep the ball, slow it down,' they [LASK] were good at Parkhead though."

Where does Celtic's loss rank amongst their worst defeats in history?

Brazil then declared that the 5-1 loss on the night will go down as one of the Hoops' worst in European football.

He said: "In the importance of the game and the money side of it, probably the worst, I would suggest.

"I was screaming at the telly, the first leg, 'We need a third, we need a third, we need a third,' and we got it.

"And then when McGregor scores an away goal, you think, 'OK, done, it's going to be backs against the wall, but it should be enough,' shocking.

4 LASK have inflicted arguably Celtic's darkest day in European football Credit: Getty

"I don't want to be too harsh on players, because it's early on in the season, but if you got to look at some of the characters and say, 'Hold on a minute, do you want to play Champions League football? Do you want to play? Do you want it that much?'

"Or is it, 'A bit unlucky, they're a good side...'"

Celtic will now be looking to return to winning ways when they host Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership on Saturday.

Sports.title: Frank Lampard handed instant survival boost as new signing backed to make big Premier League impact
Sports.content:
New Coventry signing Sidiki Cherif has been tipped to make a big impact in the Premier League this season.

Frank Lampard landed the 19-year-old striker from Fenerbahce for around £20m.



3 Cherif joined Coventry from Fenerbahce Credit: Getty

Cherif only joined Fener on a permanent deal this summer, with his loan from French side Angers including a mandatory purchase agreement.

He scored two goals in 12 Super Lig games after joining in January - but there is plenty of unrealised potential.

talkSPORT’s European football expert Andy Brassell said: “I personally think he will make a big, big impact in the Premier League. He was good when he arrived at Fenerbahce.



“Given that he was, because of their failure to sign any other senior strikers, immediately a senior striker, there's a lot to his game.

“He's really smart. But generally speaking, it's a big leap.”

Coventry have spent more than £100m this summer in a bid to stay in the Premier League after more than two decades away.



Their season got off to a tough start with a 3-0 defeat at defending champions Arsenal in what will likely be their hardest test of the campaign.

talkSPORT has been told that Lampard is not overly worried by that outing and there are plenty of positives to take.



Wrexham want Angers star

Another player who could be heading to English football via the Angers development route is Jacques Ekomie.

Wrexham are believed to have had a bid in the region of £8m for the left-back accepted, having faced competition from Championship rivals.

3 Ekomie is a target for Wrexham this summer Credit: AFP

The 23-year-old has made 36 Ligue 1 appearances since joining Angers from Bordeaux in July 2024.



Brassell warned there is a steep learning curve for all players joining from the French league as the traditional routes to step up are becoming increasingly tough.

He continued: “We've seen how difficult it is for defenders to adapt to the Premier League. We've seen how difficult it is from the very start.

“Angers is a bigger leap than Lyon. Ideally, Lyon are one of the better teams in the division.

I know the French League isn't as moneyed as it was. Not that it was ever replete with cash, but it's flat broke at the moment.



“Players going from Angers to hit that next level, that is a big ask. You are probably better off going to Marseille first, or Lyon or somewhere like that.

3 Lampard has signed a number of talented players this summer at Coventry Credit: Getty

“The problem being that Marseille and Lyon don't have the money to take you if you're a really good player at the moment.

“Angers are really, really good at developing players.”

Sports.title: Wrexham told new club-record signing would instantly be best player in the Championship
Sports.content:
Wrexham told new club-record signing would instantly be best player in the Championship

Wrexham target Pavel Sulc would immediately become the best player in the Championship if he joins.

That’s the verdict of European football expert Andy Brassell amid links to the 25-year-old Lyon forward.



4 Sulc joined Lyon from Viktoria Plzen in 2025 Credit: Getty

Czech Republic international Sulc scored 14 goals in all competitions for the Ligue 1 club last season.

Wrexham are reportedly plotting a club-record bid for the 2025 Czech player of the year.

They have already broken that this summer, signing goalkeeper Anthony Patterson from Sunderland for £8m.



This could soon be dwarfed by any transfer for Sulc as the Red Dragons look for more firepower to send them into the Premier League.

Speaking to talkSPORT.com, Brassell said: “Lyon paid €7.5m and he has just been a massive, massive hit. When you look at the sort of players who traditionally thrive in France, he probably shouldn't have been one.



“He’s a forward player, traditionally a second striker. He was sold as an attacking midfielder, but he played as a second striker or false nine. He's done it so well, considering he's built like a sparrow.

“He's had a lot of attention from defenders, but he's smart enough to avoid it.



“He makes great runs. He's technically very adept and considering that he's not the biggest guy, it's actually quite difficult to shove off the ball.

“I think you'd look at someone of that height and build and you'd think, he's not going to do it in the Championship.

“But I think he would. I really think he would. In terms of technical quality, he would be, if not the best player in the division, pretty close because he was one of the better players in Ligue 1 last season.

4 Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson is looking for more signings before deadline day Credit: Getty



“They say don't judge people by their friends. Well, firstly, you really should judge people by their friends. Secondly, the way he clicked with Endrick was notable.

“Technically, they're on a level where they can just understand each other. They played really well for a bit until Sulc got injured in the back half of last season.

“That hung over the end of his season and the World Cup and his preseason. Even though he's had his moments in all of those.

“Bear in mind, without Sulc, they wouldn't have got to the World Cup because he is a technically very gifted player in a quite average Czech team, if we're talking about the standards of their best teams. They've had some unreal players down the years."



Why do Lyon need to sell?

Lyon were initially demoted to Ligue 2 in 2025 over their mounting financial problems, but this was later overturned.

The main issue was a debt of €541 million owed by the club and a massively inflated wage bill without much cash flow.

4 Sulc featured for the Czech Republic at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty

John Textor, Lyon's owner via his holding company the Eagle Football Group and the club's president, was forced to step down from the board and his role of president by his associates.



Michele Kang, a shareholder in Eagle Football Group and successful businesswoman, is now in charge.

“It's funny because when Lyon bought him, it was a bit of a surprise,” Brassell added.

“It was really an expression of where they are in terms of the transfer market, that they don't have much money post-Textor. They are not going fishing in the major leagues.

“They don't sign players for over €10 million these days. Even if they do, they have to sell to balance the books.



“Sulc is a player who, when he came in, everyone was a little bit perplexed because he's from Czech football. It felt like a bit of a leap.

“Traditionally, really good Czech players tend to go to the bottom half of the Bundesliga. It was an expression of where Lyon were in terms of their financial means.”

Lyon in the Champions League

Despite those well publicised financial interests, Lyon qualified for the Champions League.

They play their second play-off leg against Fenerbahce, for a place in the group stage, on Wednesday.



Despite this, the club will likely need to make more sales before the transfer window closes.

4 Wrexham have drawn their opening two Championship games Credit: Getty

Brassell continued: “It was reported about a week ago that even if they do qualify for the Champions League in the playoff against Fenerbahce this week, they'll have to sell one.

“It's probably down to Sulc or Malek Fofana. Either of whom they could turn a very nice profit on from what they originally paid.



“Fofana has made it clear that he wants to stay if they make the Champions League.

“Fofana is a very, very high-level player, but last season was completely ruined by injury. He's had a few little problems, a few big problems actually, trying to come back from that as well and it forced him to miss the World Cup in the summer.

“Lyon’s plan was for him to have a good World Cup and then to sell him after. That obviously didn't work out because of the injury.

“I think he understands go out there, really get my value up by doing good stuff in the Champions League.



“The clubs that have been interested in Fofana before - we're talking about Chelsea. We're talking about Bayern, the sort of clubs who would be in for him.

“If he shows he can reach that level again, they'll be back for him in summer 2027 after he's done a good job for Lyon this season.

“From Lyon's perspective, it would probably be a little bit preferable to sell Sulc as well because Fofana is more difficult to replace.

“If Wrexham offer the sort of money that Lyon are looking for for Pavel Sulc, that would be an enormous statement of intent.”

Sports.title: Sheffield Wednesday forward Harry Gray forced off with head injury after nasty fall
Sports.content:
Sheffield Wednesday forward Harry Gray forced off with head injury after nasty fall

Sheffield Wednesday's Harry Gray suffered a head injury on Tuesday night after a nasty fall during their clash with Wolves.

Gray had to be treated by medical staff and was eventually substituted after appearing to hit his head on the floor.



2 Gray suffered a nasty injury against Wolves in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday Credit: Getty

The 17-year-old forward, who is on loan at Hillsborough from Leeds, was reported to be responsive following the incident.

He suffered the injury in the final five minutes of the Carabao Cup second-round match that Wolves won 2-0.

Journalist for the Sheffield Star, Alex Miller, wrote on X: "Harry Gray has been taken off with a head injury.



"[He] landed awkwardly and bashed his head on the floor, I think.

"He seemed to be responsive and okay, but medics were absolutely right to take swift precautions."

In reaction, one Sheffield Wednesday fan posted: "The way he walked off did not look very good at all, hope he's alright."



Another said: "He's been promising.... hope the lad's okay."

Owls manager Henrik Pedersen then revealed that there is a chance Gray's injury could be a broken nose.

He said post-match: "We don't know if the nose is broken, but we should take him out and let's see."



Sheffield Wednesday out of the cup

Sheffield Wednesday lost Gray, brother of Tottenham's Archie Gray, in the final moments of their Carabao Cup defeat to Wolves.

2 Sheffield Wednesday were knocked out of the cup by Wolves in the second round Credit: Getty

The League One outfit were beaten 2-0 by their Championship opponents after an own goal by Sil Swinkels and a first-half stoppage-time finish from Saheed Olangunju.

Pedersen's side have had a mixed start to the new campaign, having been relegated to the third tier last season.



They won their Carabao Cup first round tie against Bolton and then their League One opener against Leyton Orient, but went on to lose at home to Bradford last Thursday evening.

And now, after defeat to Wolves, they've now lost a second consecutive game at Hillsborough.

Next up for the Owls is another home game, this time against Bromley, who they will hope to beat to return to winning ways.

Sheffield Wednesday won't want Gray to be missing, as he has started every game of the season so far for them.

Sports.title: Celtic out of Champions League as they blow 4-0 aggregate lead in ‘one of the worst results in club’s history’
Sports.content:
Celtic out of Champions League as they blow 4-0 aggregate lead in ‘one of the worst results in club’s history’

Celtic's Champions League aspirations have been dashed in the most humiliating of fashions.

The Hoops lost their Champions League play-off tie to LASK 5-4 on aggregate after the Austrian outfit won the second leg 5-1.

3 LASK overcame a four-goal deficit to eliminate Celtic from the Champions League play-offs Credit: Getty

To make matters worse for Celtic, they scored the opening goal in Tuesday's encounter, meaning they boasted a four-goal lead on aggregate.

Yet that was still not enough of a cushion as LASK levelled the contest in normal time before Samuel Adeniran scored the all-important fifth goal on the night in extra time.

LASK could have had a sixth on the night when they won a penalty with five minutes remaining, but Adeniran - who would have had a hat-trick if he scored - had his effort stopped by Viljami Sinisalo.

The result marks the second-straight season the Hoops have fallen in the Champions League play-offs, meaning they will yet again drop into the Europa League.

Adding extra salt into the wounds of Celtic following the loss to LASK is the money they have left on the table.

Had they beaten LASK and qualified for the league phase of the Champions League, the Hoops would have landed a guaranteed £16million pay day.

Instead, teams who compete in the league phase of the Europa League stand to make a guaranteed £3.7m.

Jamie O'Hara and Jason Cundy react to Celtic's embarrassing loss

Upon hearing LASK had taken the lead on aggregate, talkSPORT's Sports Bar co-hosts Jason Cundy and Jamie O'Hara could not believe what had unfolded in Austria.

"What are Celtic doing? Disaster," O'Hara said when LASK's decisive goal went in.

"What are they doing? How can you lose a game when you're winning 4-0? That'll cost them a fortune... one of the worst results in Celtic's history," O'Hara added at full time.

3 Celtic will now compete in the Europa League for a second-straight season Credit: Getty

"This is one of the biggest disasters in Celtic's history," Sports Bar co-host Cundy added.

What did Celtic captain Callum McGregor say about the loss to LASK?

Hoops skipper Callum McGregor was equally stunned at how his side threw away a spot in this season's Champions League.

Speaking after the contest, McGregor admitted Celtic 'got what we deserved'.

"We looked scared to go and win the game," McGregor added.

"To be honest I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either and kind of got away with it.

"When you play like that, you can't have any excuse whatsoever.

3 O'Neill watched his side capitulate in real time against LASK Credit: Getty

"We apologise to our supporters and the club because there is no way we should lose that game."

When do Celtic play next?

Celtic will look to put Tuesday's nightmare behind them when they return to action against Falkirk.

Martin O'Neill's side have won their opening two Scottish Premiership fixtures while Falkirk have drawn once and lost once.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and possessing laughing gas after car crash
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and possessing laughing gas after car crash

Raheem Sterling is at risk of jail time after he was charged with dangerous driving by police.

The former Chelsea winger was also charged with possession of laughing gas and failing to provide a specimen following a car crash in May.

3 Sterling was last on the books of Dutch club Feyenoord Credit: Getty

Sterling's Lamborghini was seen swerving across the M3 by concerned motorists, who immediately called police.

He was subsequently arrested near an interchange just outside of Farnborough.

Police statement on Raheem Sterling

A Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman said: “A driver will appear in court next month to face charges following a collision on the M3.

“Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

“The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange, on 28 May, 2026.

“No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported.

“Mr Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court on 15 September.”

If Sterling is convicted of dangerous driving, he could face up to two years in prison.

Laughing gas, also known as hippy crack, was declared illegal in November 2023.

Repeat serious users of the class C controlled substance can also face up to two years in prison, while dealers of the drug could be jailed for up to 14 years.

3 Sterling will learn his fate over a car accident in September Credit: Getty

Raheem Sterling's career at a glance

Sterling is currently a free agent after he departed Dutch club Feyenoord at the end of the 2025/26 season.

The 31-year-old made just eight appearances for Feyenoord, failing to score and registering just one assist.

Sterling moved to the Eredivisie outfit after Chelsea terminated his contract last January a whopping 18 months ahead of schedule.

Prior to Sterling's exit, he had not featured for the Blues since May 2024 having spent the 2024/25 season on loan at Arsenal.

Sterling joined Chelsea from Manchester City for £50million in the summer of 2022 but struggled to live up to his price tag, registering just 19 goals and 15 assists in 81 games for the west London side.

His attacking output was a marked decline from the numbers he put up throughout his time at City, where he won four Premier League titles, five Carabao Cups and the FA Cup.

3 Sterling played the best football of his career under Pep Guardiola Credit: Getty

During his seven-year stay at the Etihad Stadium, Sterling scored 131 goals and provided 87 assists in 339 appearances across all competitions.

Sterling's best campaign for City came in the 2018/19 season, as he achieved 27 goal contributions in the Premier League.

The 31-year-old's exploits that season earned him the Football Writers' Association's Footballer of the Year award, the PFA Young Player of the Year award and a spot in the PFA's Premier League Team of the Year.

Sports.title: Aston Villa expect Al Hilal to pay £50m asking price for Watkins, Liverpool explore other options with Brighton wanting £80m for Minteh and all options remain open for Grealish: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Aston Villa expect Al Hilal to pay £50m asking price for Watkins, Liverpool explore other options with Brighton wanting £80m for Minteh and all options remain open for Grealish: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Aston Villa expect Saudis to meet £50m Watkins asking price

Aston Villa expect Al Hilal to hit their valuation of £50million for Ollie Watkins if they complete a deal for the England forward.

Watkins is keen to move to the Saudi Pro League club, who are offering a salary far higher than his current wages at Villa.

Villa have so far stuck to their position on Watkins and there is growing optimism Al Hilal, who have already had four bids turned down, will eventually meet the asking price.

Villa are also pursuing the £65million signing of Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea, who would effectively replace Watkins.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Monaco join queue for Spurs star Matar Sarr
