The group includes private lenders Kapital Bank and PASHA Bank. Banks linked to the family control a significant share of Azerbaijan’s banking-sector assets — more than 40%, according to some estimates. SOCAR: Azerbaijan’s state oil company is also entering Uzbekistan’s retail fuel market and plans to establish a network of filling stations there. At the same time, the company plans to cooperate with BP and Uzbekneftegaz on the Ustyurt field. SOCAR has also faced questions over transparency in the past, including in connection with the Azerbaijani Laundromat scandal.

Azerbaijan’s state oil company is also entering Uzbekistan’s retail fuel market and plans to establish a network of filling stations there. At the same time, the company plans to cooperate with BP and Uzbekneftegaz on the Ustyurt field. SOCAR has also faced questions over transparency in the past, including in connection with the Azerbaijani Laundromat scandal. Other projects: Other businesses entering the Uzbek market include the Matanat-A gypsum plant, Landau STEAM schools, the Sur gold and silver processing plant, Gold Fresh Fruits orchards, the Baku City residential complex and other projects. Some are being implemented as public-private partnerships.

Statements by the two presidents

President Ilham Aliyev said in a statement to the press that relations between the two countries were built “on a very solid foundation, both spiritually and materially”. He said the range of projects under discussion in energy, transport, investment, tourism, mining, automotive manufacturing, agriculture, processing and banking gave the cooperation an “unprecedented character”.

Aliyev said that on every visit he was struck by the rapid development of Tashkent and Uzbekistan as a whole. He said increasing bilateral trade to $1bn was “no longer a dream of the distant future, but a target that can be achieved within a few years”. He also highlighted Mirziyoyev’s particular role in attracting investment to Karabakh and invited him to make a state visit to Azerbaijan at a time convenient to him.

Shavkat Mirziyoyev described Aliyev’s visit as a “historic event”, saying the “Treaty on Eternal Friendship” was evidence of this and that the provisions on strategic partnership and alliance were being backed up by concrete action. In his remarks, he highlighted a threefold increase in bilateral trade over the past five years, the goal of raising it to $1bn, the joint development of the Middle Corridor, and the idea of creating a separate Azerbaijani-Uzbek corridor across the Caspian Sea with a single operator.

Mirziyoyev also said the two countries spoke “with one voice” on the international stage. He described Azerbaijan’s full participation in the consultative meetings of Central Asian heads of state as a historic step and praised Aliyev’s policy of restoring Azerbaijan’s territorial integrity, as well as the meeting in Washington and the declaration signed there.

Hikmet Hajiyev, a representative of the Azerbaijani presidential administration, said before and during the visit that relations between the two countries had reached a new level: moving from strategic partnership to alliance and then to “eternal friendship”. He said this was the first such step in the history of Azerbaijani diplomacy. According to Hajiyev, the “eternal friendship” that had already existed de facto between the two peoples had now been formally enshrined at the political level as well.

World.title: Kyrgyzstan, U.S. discuss expanding trade, economic, and investment ties
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 26. Kyrgyzstan and the United States discussed prospects for expanding trade, economic, and investment cooperation, with a focus on joint projects in key sectors.

This was announced in a statement by the press service of the Kyrgyz MFA, following the meeting between Ambassador to the United States Edil Baisalov and Assistant Secretary of Commerce and Director General of the United States and Foreign Commercial Service for the International Trade Administration (ITA) at the U.S. Department of Commerce, David L. Fogel.

"During the meeting, the sides discussed prospects for expanding trade, economic and investment cooperation between Kyrgyzstan and the United States," the statement said.

According to the Ministry, in the course of the meeting, particular attention was paid to opportunities for implementing joint projects in mining, banking and information technology.

Edil Baisalov briefed the US official on economic reforms being carried out in Kyrgyzstan and measures aimed at improving the country's investment climate. He emphasized the importance of diversifying the Kyrgyz economy, introducing modern technologies and attracting US investment and expertise.

The sides noted significant untapped potential for strengthening direct ties between the business communities of the two countries and expressed interest in further expanding the presence of US companies in the Kyrgyz market.

Following the meeting, the sides outlined further practical steps to promote mutually beneficial projects and continue substantive dialogue between the Kyrgyz side and the US Department of Commerce.

World.title: Tokayev calls for action against aggressive fast-food advertising
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 26. President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev instructed the government to thoroughly examine the issue of aggressive fast-food advertising, particularly its impact on children's health.

This was announced by the press service of the Kazakh President, citing Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's remarks at the plenary session of the Republican August Conference.

"Another issue is aggressive fast-food advertising that has flooded public spaces. It creates persistent unhealthy habits, increases pressure on the healthcare system and negatively affects the country's workforce potential," Tokayev said.

He noted that around 7,000 children with diabetes are currently under medical supervision in Kazakhstan, adding that the number is not declining and is even increasing.

"Many countries prohibit or restrict advertising of foods high in fat, sugar and salt aimed at younger generations," the president said.

Tokayev acknowledged that the issue is complex and involves a range of sensitive aspects, including medical and political considerations.

"However, the government still needs to thoroughly examine this issue, bearing in mind, above all, the health of our children," he said.

Tokayev also stressed the importance of protecting the psychological well-being of the younger generation. According to the president, psychological well-being, emotional resilience and the moral development of the younger generation have already become important factors of national security and sustainable development.

World.title: Tajikistan holds international conference marking 35 years of independence
World.content:
Photo: Press Service of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Tajikistan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 26. Tajikistan held an international conference on the country's experience in peacebuilding, foreign policy, and sustainable development over 35 years of independence.

This was announced by the press service of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Tajikistan.

According to the Ministry, the conference, titled "Tajikistan and 35 Years of Independence: Experience of Peacebuilding, Multivector Policy, and Sustainable Development," was held on August 25.

"On August 25, 2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Tajikistan hosted the International Conference "Tajikistan and 35 Years of Independence: Experience of Peacebuilding, Multivector Policy, and Sustainable Development" in honor of the 35th anniversary of the Republic of Tajikistan's State Independence. High-ranking representatives of the Government and Parliament of the Republic, heads of ministries and government agencies, the diplomatic corps, as well as political figures, veterans of the diplomatic service, and the country's missions abroad participated in the conference (in a virtual format)," the Ministry said.

The event brought together senior representatives of the Tajik government and parliament, heads of ministries and state agencies, members of the diplomatic corps, political figures, veterans of the diplomatic service and representatives of Tajikistan abroad, including those participating virtually.

The opening session featured remarks by First Deputy Prime Minister of Tajikistan Khokim Kholikzoda, Minister of Foreign Affairs Sirojiddin Muhriddin, the Presidential Assistant for Foreign Relations, as well as heads of several ministries and government agencies.

The thematic sessions focused on cooperation between government bodies, the academic community and the diplomatic corps in implementing the country's foreign policy, as well as the role of women in advancing the country's domestic and foreign policy.

Participants reviewed Tajikistan's achievements over 35 years of independence and discussed prospects for the country's further development.

Concluding the conference, Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin declared that the conclusions and proposals put forward during the event would contribute to further measures aimed at ensuring sustainable development and advancing Tajikistan's foreign policy.

Meanwhile, more than 200 people took part in the conference, while its proceedings were covered by 50 domestic and international media outlets.

World.title: Tokayev reveals number of schools built across Kazakhstan in five years
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 26. Kazakhstan has built 1,120 schools with more than 1 million student places over the past five years.

This was announced by the press service of the Kazakh President, citing Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's remarks at the plenary session of the Republican August Conference

According to Tokayev, education remains one of the state’s key priorities, and he emphasized the role of teachers in shaping society and developing human capital. Over the past seven years, funding for this sector has tripled, reaching 6.4 trillion tenge ($14 billion).

He added that the material and technical facilities of more than 5,000 rural schools have been upgraded, while over 7,000 modern specialized classrooms have been equipped.

Tokayev also highlighted the implementation of the "Keleshек Mektepteri" (Future Schools) project, launched two years ago on his instructions.

"Within the framework of this project, 217 schools for 460,000 students have been built. It would not be an exaggeration to say that a new standard of modern schools has emerged," he said.

The president emphasized that school construction will continue across Kazakhstan, particularly in areas where there is still a shortage of places.

"This is an important task of national significance. Starting next year, we need to begin this work without delay. Next year, we must ensure a high pace of construction," Tokayev said.

Furthermore, the president stressed the importance of strengthening the status of teachers and providing comprehensive support to education workers.

A special law, "On the Status of a Teacher," has been adopted, while amendments introduced this year provide additional legal and social guarantees for education workers. October 5 has also been officially designated as Teachers' Day in Kazakhstan. The state honors list includes the title "Merited Teacher of Kazakhstan," with recipients receiving a significant monetary award. Around 100 teachers have received the title so far.

Tokayev noted that three teachers have been awarded Kazakhstan's highest state honor, the "Hero of Labor of Kazakhstan," over the past three years. According to the TALIS 2024 study, Kazakhstan ranks second in terms of strengthening the professional status of teachers.

The country also ranks among the world's top five in terms of teachers' satisfaction with their salaries. Some 95% of education workers said they were satisfied with their profession, while 80% said they would choose teaching again if given the opportunity.

World.title: Kazakhstan continues large-scale modernization of government system, Tokayev says
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 26. Kazakhstan is continuing large-scale modernization of its government system and public institutions.

This was announced by the press service of the Kazakh President, citing Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's remarks at the plenary session of the Republican August Conference

"Just a few days ago, the first elections to the Kurultai were held, and their results were announced yesterday. This important political event was organized at an unprecedentedly high level," the press service says, citing Tokayev.

Tokayev praised the Central Election Commission's work, noting that advanced solutions, including artificial intelligence technologies, are being introduced into the electoral process to improve efficiency.

"The elections attracted considerable interest from foreign observers. The international community recognized the election results, confirming their full compliance with national legislation and all relevant requirements," the president said.

Furthermore, Tokayev announced that he had signed an order convening the first session of the Kurultai of the first convocation for August 28, in accordance with Article 46 of the Constitution. Political parties that secured seats in the Kurultai are expected to finalize their lists of deputies before the session.

According to Tokayev, the lists submitted by the parties include experienced professionals from various fields as well as citizens at the beginning of their political careers, including young people and members of the Presidential Youth Talent Reserve.

"Representatives of the new generation have undoubtedly brought new momentum to the electoral campaign. Equal opportunities were provided to everyone who seeks to serve the people honestly, is not afraid of responsibility, and thinks innovatively. Essentially, this is a natural and evolutionary process," he said.

The president also highlighted the activity, ideological preparedness and professionalism of political parties during the election campaign.

"During the election campaign, many constructive proposals were put forward that could have a direct impact on the country's future," Tokayev said.

He added that voters had also actively participated in the political process by openly expressing their views on various issues during nationwide televised debates and public discussions in the information space.

"Thus, the values of mutual respect, responsibility and pluralism of opinions are becoming increasingly rooted in society, while a new political culture is taking shape," the president said.

World.title: Governor of Russia's Astrakhan region sends congratulatory letter to First Vice President Mehriban Aliyeva
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 26. Igor Babushkin, Governor of the Astrakhan Region of the Russian Federation, sent a congratulatory letter to Mehriban Aliyeva, First Vice President of Azerbaijan.

''Dear Mehriban Arifovna,

Please accept my deepest respect and sincere congratulations on the occasion of your birthday.

I wish you robust health, prosperity, inexhaustible energy, happiness, and continued success in your multifaceted activities.

I express my sincere gratitude to you for your support in strengthening cooperation between the Astrakhan Region and the Republic of Azerbaijan.

I am confident that bilateral interaction will continue to develop successfully, creating opportunities for the implementation of new joint initiatives and projects,'' the letter reads.

World.title: PMCG says financial infrastructure key to unlocking Middle Corridor investment potential
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 26. The full development of the Middle Corridor will require not only physical infrastructure but also a developed financial infrastructure capable of attracting private investment, PMCG President Alex Aleksishvili said.

Aleksishvili made the remarks at the 10th CAREC Think Tank Development Forum in Tashkent, according to consulting company PMCG.

According to World Bank estimates, cited by Aleksishvili, trade volumes along the corridor could triple by 2030 and transport times could be cut in half with the right investments and efficiency improvements.

Trade between Azerbaijan, Georgia and Kazakhstan is expected to increase by 37%, while their trade with the European Union could rise by 28%.

Growth in trade flows will create demand not only for major transport infrastructure, but also for related facilities, Aleksishvili said.

“Rail infrastructure will require terminals, rolling stock and warehousing capacity, while ports will need logistics and processing facilities. Energy networks will require new capacity to support generation and industry. The development of digital connectivity, in turn, will drive demand for technology and data infrastructure,” he said.

Aleksishvili stressed that many of these investments cannot be financed solely through traditional bank lending.

Financial systems in Central Asia and the South Caucasus remain largely dependent on bank financing, he said.

“The problem is therefore not only a lack of capital, but also insufficient access to appropriate forms of financing,” Aleksishvili said.

Private equity, mezzanine financing, private debt and hybrid financial instruments could help bridge the gap, he said.

“These instruments can provide longer-term and more flexible financing for companies planning expansion, investing in fixed assets or implementing projects with a higher level of risk,” the PMCG president said.

World.title: Uzbekistan’s investment inflow tops $160B as economy expands
World.content:
Photo: the official channel of the Press Secretary of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 26. Uzbekistan has attracted more than $160 billion in foreign investment over the past decade, while the country’s economy has grown more than 2.5-fold, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev said, highlighting the scale of economic and social transformation carried out in recent years.

This was reflected on the official channel of the Press Secretary of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, following the ceremony on the occasion of the 35th anniversary of our country's Independence attended by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

Speaking about the results of the past 10 years, Mirziyoyev said Uzbekistan’s economy has been growing steadily and at a rapid pace as the government works alongside the population to implement reforms.

“More than $160 billion in foreign investment has entered our country over the past period. Our economy has increased by more than 2.5 times,” Mirziyoyev said.

Uzbekistan’s gross domestic product is expected to exceed $180 billion this year, he added.

The president also highlighted employment gains, saying 5.7 million permanent jobs have been created in the industrial, services and agricultural sectors.

Public-private investment has also expanded social infrastructure, with modern schools providing 1.2 million places, kindergartens with 342,000 places and hospitals with 62,000 places commissioned during the period.

The country has also invested heavily in transportation and utilities. Some 83,000 kilometers of public roads have been built or rehabilitated to improve connectivity, while centralized drinking water has been provided for the first time to households serving 8 million people.

Water supplies have also been improved for an additional 11.5 million people, according to the president.

Housing construction has been another major focus. Over the past decade, 650,000 families have moved into new modern homes, benefiting at least 2.5 million people.

“Having a home means having a homeland,” Mirziyoyev said, citing a traditional Uzbek saying.

The figures underscore the breadth of Uzbekistan’s economic and social development over the past decade, with investment, industrial growth, infrastructure expansion and improved access to basic services forming key pillars of the country’s reform program.

World.title: Court releases notes allegedly penned by accused parent murderer
World.content:
A woman standing trial accused of murdering her elderly parents allegedly scrawled notes — which a court has released — including a reference to police waiting to see if she would "get cocky and slip up".

Raelene Polymiadis, 65, of Craigmore is standing trial in South Australia's Supreme Court, after pleading not guilty to murdering her parents, Brenda and Lynton Anderson, by injecting them with her own insulin in 2022 and 2023.

Prosecutors previously told the jury a set of notes were allegedly found during a search of Ms Polymiadis's house and car and detailed what she should be saying to police when she spoke to them.

Brenda and Lynton Anderson, both aged 94, died a year apart. (Supplied: Nine News)

Supreme Court Justice Sandi McDonald, who is presiding over the trial, approved the release of handwritten notes, which prosecutors alleged were penned by Ms Polymiadis.

One note written on the top corner of a piece of paper said: "What they will do is wait for a few weeks months year to see if I think I got away with it and I get cocky and slip up. Hang on buddy, it could be a long ride."

A handwritten note tendered in the Raelene Polymiadis murder trial. (Supplied: Courts SA)

In another note, the author posed questions to authorities.

"Who are you sorry?" the note read.

"What's this about?

"Are you from the Coroner's office?

"Why only now are you speaking with me and it's only a few days after the funeral!!"

One of the handwritten notes released by the Supreme Court lists questions. (Supplied: Courts SA)

Prosecutors previously told the court Ms Polymiadis wrote to herself to "sob here", saying that matched a point in the police interview where she started sobbing.

One of the notes released by the court discussed events occurring in hospital.

"We went to see dad, they were keeping him warm," part of the note said.

"He was out to it — unconscious I guess but breathing with help of oxygen I 'think' — I'm sorry this is really hard relieving all this — is it absolutely necessary."

Another handwritten note prosecutors allege Raelene Polymiadis wrote. (Supplied: Courts SA)

The note went on to say, "… just holding his hand, talking to him, but I got no response (sob)".

The trial previously heard police listening devices captured Ms Polymiadis in her car praying to God, confessing to the crimes.

Ms Polymiadis's lawyer, Marie Shaw KC, previously told the jury the context of the alleged confession would arise during the trial.

"The issue about the alleged confession is: was my client admitting she was responsible for the deaths or was she telling her god she felt responsible for their deaths because if they died of insulin administration, they must have accessed her insulin?" Ms Shaw said.

Another of the handwritten notes tendered in the Raelene Polymiadis murder trial. (Supplied: Courts SA)

Another note made references to Ms Polymiadis's father.

"Then I burst into tears, thinking my God he got into my stuff, it's my fault."

The trial continues.

World.title: Canberra childcare centre ordered to close as provider enters administration
World.content:
The childcare regulator has ordered Edge Early Learning in Charnwood in Canberra's Belconnen area to close for three months.

The notice of suspension, issued by Children's Education and Care Assurance (CECA), comes about a month after an Edge Early Learning centre in nearby Higgins was forced to shut immediately over its response to a serious medical incident involving a child.

The reasons behind the Charnwood centre's notice of suspension remain unknown, with its closure due to begin on September 3.

In a statement, CECA said:

"Edge has the right to appeal the decision and is legally required to communicate the suspension to families. "Under administration, the administrator can also exercise the right to appeal."

The ABC has spoken to parents who said they were unaware that CECA had ordered the Charnwood centre to close for three months from next Thursday.

Edge Early Learning also has a centre operating in Ngunnawal in the Gungahlin area.

The Edge Early Learning centre in the ACT that was forced to close suddenly in July. (ABC News: Matt Roberts)

'Business-as-usual'

It comes as the childcare provider, which runs dozens of childcare centres across South Australia, Queensland and the ACT, went into voluntary administration.

In a statement from Edge Early Learning, it said administrators had been appointed to "review the business and work with key stakeholders to determine the best path forward", and that the process would allow the company "to assess its financial position and consider options for its future".

" We understand that this may be a confusing and stressful development for families who rely upon Edge Early Learning to provide care for their children. "

Canberra childcare centre ordered to close A Canberra mother had concerns for her daughter's safety at Edge Early Learning in Higgins long before the ACT regulator ordered the centre to close.

Edge Early Learning said it was continuing to operate all centres "on a business-as-usual basis".

"There will be no change to your care arrangements, centre opening hours or staffing. Families should continue to attend their centre as normal," it told parents.

"Our immediate focus is to maintain the safe and ongoing operation of each centre while this urgent review is undertaken."

World.title: Body found as police investigate shooting of Melbourne father
World.content:
Homicide detectives have found a body in their search for a Melbourne father who went missing after allegedly being shot.

A desperate search has been underway for Khaled Malas, 37, who has not been seen since he was allegedly attacked at a home in Wildwood, north-west of the city, on August 19.

Police allege he was shot after a dispute, which is understood to involve a significant debt, and there were grave fears for his welfare.

Police last week searched near a waste facility at Sunbury for missing man Khaled Malas. (ABC News)

Mohammed Aboueid, 56, has been charged with intentionally causing serious injury.

On Wednesday afternoon, investigators found human remains covered in grass on Havelock Road in Clarkefield, about 15 kilometres from Wildwood.

The coroner has been notified, and an autopsy is expected to take place.

Victoria Police said it would consider alternative charges upon receiving the results of the autopsy.

Mr Malas has been remembered as a loving father.

World.title: Queensland allowed to use coal, gas for data centres despite renewable push
World.content:
Queensland will be allowed to go its own way using gas or coal to power data centres, despite Prime Minister Anthony Albanese previously demanding states use renewables.

State and territory leaders met on Wednesday to settle national standards for data centre construction, but instead agreed to undertake further work.

Queensland Premier Crisafulli had pushed for an energy-agnostic approach and told the ABC the carve out was a "good win" for his state, which owns much of its own electricity infrastructure.

Data centre fight heats up Premiers are heading into national cabinet divided over how Australia should meet the rapidly growing energy demands of AI data centres.

"It shows because we own our assets, both our distribution and our generation, we are able to control a different mixture of energy right across the board, and that enables us to bring on new energy opportunities," he said.

Premiers and chief ministers met with Mr Albanese in Sydney to discuss issues including AI, domestic violence, bird flu, fuel security and the embattled national gun buyback.

Ahead of the meeting, federal Energy Minister Chris Bowen had insisted the Commonwealth would legislate over the top of states and territories that refused to adopt the renewables standard.

Queensland argued the state-owned nature of its energy infrastructure put it in a position to maintain a technology-agnostic approach, meaning gas or coal could be used to power its data centres.

The Northern Territory also opposed the renewables focus and has indicated it would use gas to power data centre projects.

Following the meeting, Mr Albanese said both jurisdictions were in a "different position" to other states, as he justified the apparent backdown on renewables.

Queensland Premier David Crisafulli had argued for a technology-neutral approach. (ABC News: Nick Dole)

A communique released after national cabinet said the standards would "ensure consistency and clarity for investors, while protecting Australia's economy, strengthening our sovereignty and securing benefits in line with our national interests".

The prime minister said the new standards, which would also include rules on water usage and community consultation, would be legislated early next year.

"We have buy-in on Australia's first national AI laws," he said.

Ongoing discussions are expected to include ensuring data centres do not raise power prices for households and other businesses.

Mr Bowen has consistently argued renewables were the cheapest form of energy to ensure this did not happen.

But Mr Crisafulli has rejected this and insisted his state would be able to keep power prices low even where other energy sources were used.

"We believe that we can control our data sovereignty, protect the rights of local communities, and enable that energy mix even with those data centres on," he said.

Citizenship a condition of holding gun licence

The meeting of national cabinet also agreed to make Australian citizenship a condition of holding a firearm licence, though the prime minister indicated there would be some exceptions.

There was little movement on a national gun buyback scheme, which the federal government tried to roll out following the Bondi terrorist attack in December last year.

Queensland had refused to take part, while others including Victoria and South Australia are yet to sign up.

Albanese to override Queensland on data centres Queensland's rejection of rules tying data centre construction to new renewables projects means the federal government will be forced to legislate to override the state.

Mr Albanese said the offer was "still there", though jurisdictions were "responsible for their own decisions".

He said the new firearm agreement would allow the sharing of Commonwealth criminal intelligence with the states and territories.

"This is about improving our laws following the horrific antisemitic attack in Bondi last year," Mr Albanese said.

GST distribution was largely off the agenda after Mr Albanese declared on Tuesday he would not meddle with Western Australia's portion of the carve-up while he was prime minister, despite opposition from other jurisdictions.

Cabinet also heard a report from Australia's head vet as the federal government prepares to tip an additional $125 million to protect the nation from bird flu, which has now been detected in all six states.

World.title: Wife of key figure in ICAC probe paid $254k for three months of work
World.content:
The NSW corruption watchdog has heard that the wife of a key figure in an inquiry was paid $254,666 for three months of consulting.

The Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) is examining allegations that prohibited political donations were funnelled through third parties to support the Liberal-aligned, right-wing faction known as the NSW Reformers and advance the interests of fugitive property developer Jean Nassif.

Anita Perrottet is the wife of Charles Perrottet, a Reformers member and the brother of former NSW premier Dominic Perrottet.

Charles is a brother of former NSW premier Dominic Perrottet. (Supplied: Facebook)

ICAC is investigating payments made to Ms Perrottet's company, Macquarie Consulting, by lobbyist Jeremy Greenwood's businesses Beckington and JPG Advisory, and whether those payments were for genuine consulting work or used to disguise money allegedly intended for Charles Perrottet.

The commission heard Ms Perrottet was paid $254,666 for three months of consulting work in 2022, despite telling the inquiry she mainly provided verbal marketing and strategic advice and could recall little documentation of the work.

Counsel assisting the commission, Peggy Dwyer SC, challenged the scale of the payments, which were made through Mr Greenwood's businesses.

"That's based on a salary of $1 million, Mrs Perrottet … let's get serious," Dr Dwyer said. "You are giving evidence under oath … Do you seriously suggest that the commission should accept that as truthful evidence that you were entitled to charge $254,666 for work that you actually did … providing an oral sounding board or advice to Jeremy Greenwood for that quarter?"

Ms Perrottet insisted the evidence was truthful.

$10,000 monthly retainer

The ICAC is investigating allegations of prohibited political donations. (ABC News)

Ms Perrottet also told the commission she received a $10,000 monthly retainer from Beckington, without a written or signed agreement.

She said her work was primarily delivered through conversations with Mr Greenwood, either in person or by phone.

Dr Dwyer said the commission had found no evidence of phone calls between Ms Perrottet and Mr Greenwood during the relevant periods.

The commission heard Ms Perrottet could remember only one Beckington client, Greyhound Racing NSW, and that she gave Mr Greenwood advice about the client during face-to-face meetings but could not recall when or where those meetings occurred.

"Are you struggling to remember because it actually didn't happen?" Dr Dwyer asked.

The commission was also shown an invoice from Macquarie Consulting for $150,000, covering 12 months of work for Beckington, which was sent by Charles Perrottet.

Ms Perrottet could not remember why the invoice had been issued, why Charles Perrottet sent it or why three lump-sum payments subsequently received from Beckington did not reconcile with the $150,000 invoice.

The key figures in ICAC investigation Eight weeks of public hearings by the ICAC that could change the NSW Liberal Party forever begin on Monday.

Ms Perrottet said she could not recall the details of the fee arrangement but maintained she probably discussed it with Mr Greenwood.

The commission also heard evidence that lobbyist Christian Ellis, also a key figure in the inquiry, sent Charles Perrottet instructions about how invoices from Macquarie Consulting should be structured, including the amounts and periods to be billed.

The commission has also ordered Ms Perrottet to provide phone records and messages involving Mr Greenwood and Mr Ellis as it tests her account of the consulting work.

Ms Perrottet will continue giving evidence on Friday before her husband takes the stand.

Dominic Perrottet is not accused of any wrongdoing.

World.title: Hobart council advances ban on full-home short stays
World.content:
A plan to block Hobart property owners from converting their entire homes into short-stay accommodation has passed another milestone, with the local council voting to send the proposal off for final approval.

Council revives bid to curb whole-home short-stays A fresh proposal from the Hobart City Council would block about 90 per cent of the city's homes from being wholly converted into short-stay accommodation.

The proposal, which aims to restrict the creation of new short-stay accommodation in the city, was considered by the Hobart City Council (HCC) at its planning committee meeting on Wednesday.

The tweak to planning rules would block about 20,000 homes from being wholly converted into visitor accommodation, such as Airbnb or Stayz.

"The draft amendment delivers a clear net community benefit through improved housing outcomes while still allowing the visitor economy to be accommodated," council officers wrote.

"The primary purpose of the proposed amendment is to limit the impact of new visitor accommodation use on the availability and affordability of housing for long-term residents in the city.

"It was informed by extensive background analysis, including data on housing and rental markets, tourism trends, existing visitor accommodation supply and planning approvals."

Council officers said the plan delivers a "clear net community benefit" by improving housing outcomes, while still accommodating the visitor economy. (ABC News: Kate Nickels)

More than 50 submissions were made while the plan was out for public consultation across June and July, with 15 supporting the amendment while 41 were in opposition.

The representations in support of the amendment focused largely on the impact that whole-home short stays have on the rental market, housing affordability, neighbourhood cohesion and the function of residential zoning.

Those against the amendment highlighted the benefits short stays have on the city's economy and tourism, their role in providing accommodation for workers and families, private property rights, investment certainty and the impact on small business owners.

The planning amendment will now be sent to the Tasmanian Planning Commission (TPC) for final approval, with the council anticipating a public hearing will be held.

Short stay rental host says 'hosting is an economic lifeline'

Merrydith Callegari, who has been a short-stay rental host in Hobart for more than 10 years, addressed the planning committee ahead of the vote.

She was opposed to the amendment and called for an opportunity to work constructively with the council to develop a framework where short-term rental owners and the council could work together.

"Short-term rentals are a vital part of Tasmania's accommodation requirements, hosting is an economic lifeline for many hosts and related industries, they fill gaps that hotels can't, they give visitors a home," Ms Callegari said.

"I believe banning does not give the result you seek … we need to make building easier, to support landlords, not tear them down — after all, if renting is too hard, landlords will stop renting.

" Every host should have the right to host … it allows people to earn an income they never could before. "

Councillors divided on if move will help rental crisis

Lord Mayor Anna Reynolds said cities all over the world were dealing with an increase in short-term rentals, while housing stock continued to fall short of demand.

"It's got to the stage where it's having a very significant impact on our rental market," she said.

"We are losing young people to other parts of Hobart because they can't get a rental here.

"This is rental stock that's been basically turned into small hotels in our suburbs."

Anna Reynolds says short-stay accommodation is having a "significant impact" on the city's rental market. (ABC News: Luke Bowden)

Cr Reynolds said the amendment was a "good compromise" and still allowed for permits in the CBD, while also not removing any existing permits.

Council locks in 1,050 per cent short-stay conversion fee hike A Tasmanian council has pushed through a 1,050 per cent increase in fees for applications to turn a property into short-stay accommodation.

"We have a higher penetration of short stays as a percentage of our rental market than I think any other capital city," she said.

Councillor Ben Lohberger supported the amendment and said whole-home short-stay rentals have filled some streets with "mini hotels".

"It's quite obvious to me that we do need some way to have discretion on whether we approve these and that's what this is about," he said.

"It's not about banning anything that exist, its not about banning every single future application; it's about giving the council the power to decide.

" We are simply trying to respond to a growing issue. "

Ben Lohberger says whole-home short-stays have filled some residential streets with "mini hotels". (ABC News: Luke Bowden)

Alderman Marti Zucco said property owners should be able to do whatever they wanted with their homes.

"We should be listening to those representations we got and maybe instead sit down and see if we can find another way forward," Cr Zucco said.

" This is not going to solve the rental crisis in Hobart … we've missed that boat. "

Marti Zucco says property owners should be able to do what they like with their homes. (ABC News: Luke Bowden)

Deputy Lord Mayor Zelinda Sherlock stressed that the amendment was not "about banning anything" and only applied to residential areas.

The restriction would apply to properties zoned as general residential, inner residential or low-density residential, which account for about 90 per cent of dwellings in Hobart.

The historic suburb of Battery Point, which is very popular for tourists, and Hobart's inner CBD would not be affected.

The councillors who voted in support of the proposal included Anna Reynolds, Ryan Posselt, Gemma Kitsos, Bill Harvey, Ben Lohberger, Mike Dutta and Zelinda Sherlock.

Those who voted against were Marti Zucco, Will Coats and Louise Bloomfield, while councillors Louise Elliot and John Kelly were not present.

World.title: Breaking: Macquarie Group dumps KPMG from audit contract
World.content:
Macquarie Group has announced it is parting ways with KPMG, the accounting firm currently the subject of a parliamentary inquiry over mishandled client data.

Macquarie released a statement today citing the ongoing scrutiny of KPMG and said the board held concerns over the firm's auditing practices.

"The decision follows continued scrutiny of KPMG Australia’s audit practice, including information exposed by the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Corporations and Financial Services," the statement said.

"It also follows Macquarie’s formal enquiries of KPMG to consider its capacity to deliver the audit, as well as the nature and impact of ongoing issues at KPMG Australia."

At Macquarie's 2027 Annual General Meeting, the board said they will recommend retaining PwC as the incumbent auditor.

KPMG also released a statement acknowledging the decision.

"While disappointed by the outcome, KPMG respects the decision taken by Macquarie," the statement read.

KPMG CEO John Sams said Macquarie's announcement was "a clear reminder that the consequences of our past failings are real".

"Rebuilding trust will require sustained action, transparency and time. I am committed to leading this change with honesty, transparency and urgency," he said.

World.title: Cream puff restaurateur avoids jail over lies to corruption watchdog
World.content:
A Sydney restaurateur has avoided jail after lying to the state's corruption watchdog to protect his brother.

Valentine Yee, 52, pleaded guilty to two counts of give false/misleading evidence at public inquiry after 2019 Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) hearings into a $100,000 donation to NSW Labor from billionaire property developer Huang Xiangmo.

Yee initially told the ICAC inquiry he had donated $5,000 to Labor using "lucky money", before admitting to signing a false declaration document to help disguise the true origin of the 2015 donation.

He told the corruption watchdog he was "helping my brother, Jonathan", who was at that time the president of Chinese Friends of Labor.

Yee's parents own and operate Chinatown yum cha institution Emperor's Garden, which was mysteriously shuttered earlier this month.

The Yee family's Emperor's Garden restaurant, a Sydney institution, recently closed out of nowhere. (ABC News: Liam Patrick)

In the NSW Local Court on Wednesday, Judge John Sfinas sentenced Yee to a two-year community corrections order for what he described as two lies to ICAC, the first relating to the false $5,000 donation and the second relating to a $10,000 donation from Emperor's Garden.

The maximum penalty for giving false or misleading evidence to ICAC is five years' imprisonment.

Judge Sfinas said he had taken into account that Yee was remorseful, that the lies were at the lower end of objective seriousness, that he had no criminal history and that the prosecution had been looming over him for one-eighth of his life.

However, he said the conviction itself was serious.

"While you have sought to explain your conduct, it is egregious conduct because it is lying to ICAC … I accept it is your brother you were effectively lying for or with, but when you lie to ICAC it effectively allows for corruption in this state to go uncovered," Judge Sfinas said.

Valentine Yee leaving the Downing Centre Local Court on Tuesday. (ABC News)

Before Yee's sentencing, defence barrister James Glissan KC submitted that Yee had not been motivated by personal gain but "a misplaced and completely fatuous, frankly, loyalty to his brother".

He said Yee had corrected the record in front of ICAC and was otherwise a man of "significant integrity".

Two other people who lied to ICAC during the investigation code-named Operation Aero have been sentenced this year.

To Yip was sentenced to a two-year community corrections order in July, and Lei Mo was sentenced to nine months in prison to be served as an intensive correction order in April.

Jonathan Yee has been charged with a suite of offences and is yet to enter a plea.

His mother, May Ho Yee, has also been charged with give false/misleading evidence at public inquiry.

The Yee family are veterans of central Sydney's Chinatown. Jonathan and Valentine's father, Stanley Yee, opened the famous Emperor's Garden restaurant in 1979, which has become known for yum cha and takeaway cream puffs.

Stanley Yee is not accused of any wrongdoing.

Shut Sydney Chinatown cream puff eatery owes tax office $845,000 The 47-year-old Emperor's Garden restaurant famously attracted long queues of customers lining up for cream puffs made fresh and sold cheap from a small takeaway window.

The bakery and restaurant on Hay Street, Haymarket, closed earlier this month.

The Australian Taxation Office is pursuing the Emperor's Garden company for an alleged tax debt of more than $845,000 with a hearing set down in the Federal Court on Friday.

Emperor's Garden BBQ and Noodles, on nearby Thomas Street, remains open, but its building is listed for auction in September.

Yee declined to comment when leaving Sydney's Downing Centre on Wednesday.

World.title: Police investigating death of Sydney teenager after suspected choking act during sex
World.content:
PoliticsNSWCrime Police investigating death of Sydney teenager after suspected choking act during sex Jack Gramenz Updated August 26, 2026 — 8:03pm ,first published 3:16pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Police are investigating the death of a 16-year-old girl on Sydney’s northern beaches after a suspected choking act during sex. The teenager died in hospital two days after emergency services responded to a concern for welfare at an Elanora Heights on Sunday night. They found the girl unresponsive. Loading She was flown in a critical condition to Royal North Shore Hospital, where she died on Tuesday night. Two sources with knowledge of the case confirmed the teenager is believed to have engaged in a choking act during sex.



Warnings about sexual strangulation have increased amid scrutiny of violent online pornography, which experts say has warped young people’s understanding of sex and normalised concerning behaviour. Consent education advocate Chanel Contos said she was devastated by news of the teen’s death: “This just feels insanely preventable.” “There is no safe way to engage in strangulation during sex, and unfortunately, mainly because of pornography, where young people are learning and mimicking scripts from that, this act that was traditionally on the fringes of kink culture has made it way into the mainstream,” the Teach Us Consent founder said. “We need to seriously investigate the impact that pornography is having on shaping the sexual scripts and behaviours of young people.” Researchers at the University of Melbourne and University of Queensland reported in 2024 that about 50 per cent of young people had engaged in choking or strangulation during sex, partly because many people mistakenly believe it can be done safely.



“And there’s really no reason to think that the effects of strangulation would be any different if the strangulation was consensual or otherwise,” the study’s lead author, University of Melbourne Professor Heather Douglas, said. “Even lower levels of strangulation, it can result in brain injuries like problem-solving difficulties, memory issues, and so on, and that’s without even being made unconscious, so it’s a really serious thing to do.” “There’s such a range of injuries associated with strangulation. Some are permanent, some are fleeting … it doesn’t take much pressure, and it doesn’t take very long, to have really terrible consequences.” Douglas said there were no safe ways to undertake strangulation, and she questioned aspects of consent surrounding it. Among the almost 5000 people aged between 18 and 35 surveyed in the research were reports of consent having been assumed from previous instances of strangulation, consent without an understanding of the risks, and consent influenced by pressure or power differentials, Douglas said.



“A lot of people just want to be normal … and doing normal things in their sex life. “And I think there is a bit of a normalisation of strangulation in many young people’s sex lives,” Douglas said. The 16-year-old died at Royal North Shore Hospital on Tuesday night. Renee Nowytarger The NSW government’s own submission to a recent parliamentary inquiry said depictions of sexual aggression including strangulation in pornography has been linked to increased intimate partner violence, citing research from 2017 by the federal government’s Australian Institute of Family Studies. Federal independent MP Zali Steggall, from the neighbouring electorate of Warringah, said the teenager’s death underscored the need for a national education campaign to tackle misogyny and teach respectful relationships.



“My thoughts are with her family, friends and community at this incredibly difficult time,” she said. “Police are investigating the circumstances of the girl’s death and no charges have been laid. We must allow the legal process to take place. “Regardless of the circumstances of this particular case, the Albanese government itself has confirmed that rates of sexual violence, particularly amongst young people, are rising. “The Albanese government must urgently roll out a national campaign ensuring young people receive ongoing sexual health and relationship education.” Support is available from the National Sexual Assault, Domestic Family Violence Counselling Service at 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732).
